20:1: Surah Taha It is Meccan Imam of Imams Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah narrated in the Book of Monotheism on the authority of Ziyad bin Ayoub on the authority of Ibrahim bin Al-Mundhir Al-Hizami: Ibrahim bin Muhajir bin Mismar narrated to us on the authority of Umar bin Hafs bin Dhakwan on the authority of the client of Al-Harqa - meaning Abd Al-Rahman bin Yaqoub - on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God recited Ta Ha and Ya Seen a thousand years before He created Adam. When the angels heard them, they said: Blessed is the nation upon whom this is revealed, and blessed are the bellies that bear this, and blessed are the tongues that speak this.” This is a strange hadith and it contains something strange, and Ibrahim bin Muhajir and his sheikh were criticized for them. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful The discussion of the disconnected letters at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah has already been presented, so there is no need to repeat it here. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Shaybah Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Ahmad - meaning Al-Zubayri - told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ta-Ha, O man. And this is how it was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Ata, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Abu Malik, Atiyah Al-Awfi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and Ibn Abi Zayd that they said: Ta-Ha means O man. And in a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Saeed ibn Jubayr and Ath-Thawri, it is a Nabataean word meaning O man. Abu Salih said: It is an Arabized word. Judge Iyad narrated in his book Al-Shifa’ from the path of Abd bin Hamid in his interpretation: Hashim bin Al-Qasim narrated to us from Ibn Ja’far from Al-Rabi’ bin Anas who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he would stand on one leg and raise the other.” Then God Almighty revealed: Ta Ha meaning: “O Muhammad, step on the earth. “We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable.” Then he said: It is not hidden what is in this honor and good treatment and His saying: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable. Juwaybir said from Al-Dahhak: When God revealed the Qur’an to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, he and his companions stood up with it, and the polytheists of Quraysh said: This Qur’an was not sent down to Muhammad except to make him miserable. Then God Almighty revealed: “Ta Ha. We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable. But only as a reminder for him who fears God.” So the matter is not as the falsifiers claim, rather whoever God gives knowledge, He intends much good for him, as is proven in the two Sahihs from Mu’awiyah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God intends good for, He gives him understanding of the religion. How good is the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani in this regard, where he said: Ahmad bin Zuhair told us, Al-Ala bin Salem told us, Ibrahim Al-Talaqani told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Al-Hakam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty will say to the scholars on the Day of Resurrection when He sits on His throne to judge His servants: I did not place My knowledge and wisdom among you except that I wanted to forgive you for what you did, and I do not care.” Its chain of transmission is good, and this Tha’laba bin Al-Hakam is Al-Laythi. Abu Omar mentioned him in his book Al-I’ti’ab, and he said: He settled in Basra then moved to Kufa, and Samak bin Harb narrated from him. Mujahid said about his statement: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable it is like his statement: So recite as much of it as is easy for you and they used to hang ropes on their chests in prayer. Qatada said: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable no, by God, He did not make it miserable, but He made it a mercy, a light, and a guide to Paradise except as a reminder for him who fears God sent down His Book and sent His Messenger as a mercy with which He showed mercy to His servants so that the one who remembers may remember, and a man may benefit from what he hears from the Book of God, which is a reminder in which God has revealed what is lawful and what is unlawful. And His statement: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens meaning this Qur’an that has come to you, O Muhammad, is a revelation from your Lord, the Lord of all things and their King, who is able to do whatever He wills, who created the earth with its lowness and density, and created the high heavens with their height and softness. It was mentioned in the hadith that was authenticated by al-Tirmidhi and others that the thickness of each heaven is a journey of five hundred years, and the distance between it and the one following it is a journey of five hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here the hadith of the mountain goats on the authority of al-Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and may God be pleased with him. And His statement: The Most Gracious established Himself firmly on the Throne has been discussed previously in Surat al-A’raf, so there is no need to repeat it here either. And the safest approach in this is the approach of the Salaf, to pass on what came in the Qur’an and Sunnah regarding this without specifying, distorting, likening, disabling, or representing. And His saying: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil meaning, all of it is His, in His grasp, and under His control, will, desire and rule. He is the Creator of that, its Owner and its God, there is no god but Him and no Lord but Him. And His saying: And what is under the soil Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: meaning what is under the seventh earth. Al-Awza’i said: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told him that Ka’b was asked and it was said to him: What is under this earth? He said: Water. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the earth? He said: Water. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the earth? He said: Water. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the earth? He said: The rock. It was said: What is under the rock? He said: A king. It was said: What is under the king? He said: A whale whose two ends are attached to the throne. It was said: What is under the whale? He said: The air and darkness, and knowledge was cut off. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubaidullah bin Akhi bin Wahb told us, my uncle told us, Abdullah bin Ayyash told us, Abdullah bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Daraj, on the authority of Isa bin Hilal al-Sadfi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The two lands, between each land and the one next to it, are a journey of five hundred years. The upper one of them is on the back of a whale whose two ends meet in the sky, and the whale is on a rock, and the rock is in the hand of the angel. The second is the prison of the wind, and in the third there are the stones of Hell, and in the fourth there is the sulfur of Hell, and in the fifth there are the snakes of Hell, and in the sixth there are the scorpions of Hell, and in the seventh there is Hell, and in it Satan is chained with iron, one hand in front of him and one hand behind him. So if God wants to release him for whatever He wills, He releases him.” This is a very strange hadith, and its chaining it to the Prophet is questionable. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Harawi told us on the authority of al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl, who said: I said: Ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari? He said: Yes, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. We came back in intense heat, and we were separated into one or two people, spreading out. He said: I was at the front of the army when a man came across us and greeted us, then he said: Which of you is Muhammad? My companions went on and I stopped with him, and behold, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came in the middle of the army on a red camel, covering his head with his garment to protect him from the sun. I said: O questioner, this is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who has come to you. He said: Which of them is he? I said: The one with the red camel. He approached him and took hold of the reins of his camel, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held him back and said: Are you Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: I want to ask you about characteristics that no one on earth knows except one or two men. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask whatever you want. He said: O Muhammad, does the Prophet sleep? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: O Muhammad, how does the child resemble his father and mother? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The man’s semen is white and thick, and the woman’s semen is yellow and thin. Which of the two semens prevails over the other, the child will be born? He said: You have spoken the truth. He asked: What does the man have from the child, and what does the woman have from it? He said: The man has the bones, veins, and nerves, and the woman has the flesh, blood, and hair. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: O Muhammad, what is under this? - meaning the earth - The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Creation. He said: What is under them? He said: Earth. He said: What is under the earth? He said: Water. He said: What is under the water? He said: Darkness. He said: What is under the darkness? He said: Air. He said: What is under the air? He said: Soil. He said: What is under the soil? The eyes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, overflowed with tears, and he said: The knowledge of creation ends with the knowledge of the Creator. O questioner, the one asked about it does not know more than the questioner. He said: You have spoken the truth. I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, do you know who this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. This is what Gabriel, peace be upon him, said. This is a very strange hadith, and a strange context. Al-Qasim bin Abdul-Rahman is the only one who narrated it. Yahya bin Ma’in said about him: He is worth nothing. Abu Hatim al-Razi declared him weak, and Ibn ‘Adi said: He is not known. I said: He mixed up this hadith, and something entered into something else and a hadith into a hadith. It may be possible that he did that intentionally or that something entered into it, and God knows best. And His statement: “And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is more hidden.” That is, this Qur’an was sent down by the One who created the earth and the high heavens, the One who knows the secret and what is more hidden, as the Most High said: “Say, ‘He sent it down who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’” Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He knows the secret and what is more hidden. He said: The secret is what the son of Adam keeps secret in himself. And what is more hidden is what was hidden from the son of Adam of what he will do before he knows it. So God knows all of that, so His knowledge of what has passed of that and what remains is one knowledge, and all of creation in that regard is like one soul with Him, and this is His statement: He did not create you and resurrect you except as one soul. Ad-Dahhak said: He knows the secret and what is more hidden. He said: The secret is what your soul speaks to, and what is more hidden is what your soul has not spoken to yet. Saeed bin Jubair said: You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you conceal tomorrow. God knows what you conceal today and what you conceal tomorrow. Mujahid said: And concealed means the whispering. He and Saeed bin Jubair also said: And concealed meaning what He knows of that which He did not speak to Himself. And His statement: “God, there is no god but He. To Him belong the best names” means the One who sent down the Qur’an to you. He is God, there is no god but He, the Possessor of the best names and the highest attributes. The hadiths that were narrated about the best names were presented at the end of Surat Al-A’raf. All praise and thanks be to God.

How good is the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani in this regard, where he said: Ahmad bin Zuhair told us, Al-Ala bin Salem told us, Ibrahim Al-Talaqani told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Tha’laba bin Al-Hakam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty will say to the scholars on the Day of Resurrection when He sits on His throne to judge His servants: I did not place My knowledge and wisdom among you except that I wanted to forgive you for what you did, and I do not care.” Its chain of transmission is good, and this Tha’laba bin Al-Hakam is Al-Laythi. Abu Omar mentioned him in his book Al-I’ti’ab, and he said: He settled in Basra then moved to Kufa, and Samak bin Harb narrated from him. Mujahid said about his statement: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable it is like his statement: So recite as much of it as is easy for you and they used to hang ropes on their chests in prayer. Qatada said: We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable no, by God, He did not make it miserable, but He made it a mercy, a light, and a guide to Paradise except as a reminder for him who fears God sent down His Book and sent His Messenger as a mercy with which He showed mercy to His servants so that the one who remembers may remember, and a man may benefit from what he hears from the Book of God, which is a reminder in which God has revealed what is lawful and what is unlawful. And His statement: A revelation from Him who created the earth and the high heavens meaning this Qur’an that has come to you, O Muhammad, is a revelation from your Lord, the Lord of all things and their King, who is able to do whatever He wills, who created the earth with its lowness and density, and created the high heavens with their height and softness. It was mentioned in the hadith that was authenticated by al-Tirmidhi and others that the thickness of each heaven is a journey of five hundred years, and the distance between it and the one following it is a journey of five hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned here the hadith of the mountain goats on the authority of al-Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and may God be pleased with him. And His statement: The Most Gracious established Himself firmly on the Throne has been discussed previously in Surat al-A’raf, so there is no need to repeat it here either. And the safest approach in this is the approach of the Salaf, to pass on what came in the Qur’an and Sunnah regarding this without specifying, distorting, likening, disabling, or representing. And His saying: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil meaning, all of it is His, in His grasp, and under His control, will, desire and rule. He is the Creator of that, its Owner and its God, there is no god but Him and no Lord but Him. And His saying: And what is under the soil Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: meaning what is under the seventh earth. Al-Awza’i said: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told him that Ka’b was asked and it was said to him: What is under this earth? He said: Water. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the earth? He said: Water. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the earth? He said: Water. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the water? He said: The earth. It was said: What is under the earth? He said: The rock. It was said: What is under the rock? He said: A king. It was said: What is under the king? He said: A whale whose two ends are attached to the throne. It was said: What is under the whale? He said: The air and darkness, and knowledge was cut off. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubaidullah bin Akhi bin Wahb told us, my uncle told us, Abdullah bin Ayyash told us, Abdullah bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Daraj, on the authority of Isa bin Hilal al-Sadfi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The two lands, between each land and the one next to it, are a journey of five hundred years. The upper one of them is on the back of a whale whose two ends meet in the sky, and the whale is on a rock, and the rock is in the hand of the angel. The second is the prison of the wind, and in the third there are the stones of Hell, and in the fourth there is the sulfur of Hell, and in the fifth there are the snakes of Hell, and in the sixth there are the scorpions of Hell, and in the seventh there is Hell, and in it Satan is chained with iron, one hand in front of him and one hand behind him. So if God wants to release him for whatever He wills, He releases him.” This is a very strange hadith, and its chaining it to the Prophet is questionable. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Harawi told us on the authority of al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl, who said: I said: Ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari? He said: Yes, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: “I was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. We came back in intense heat, and we were separated into one or two people, spreading out. He said: I was at the front of the army when a man came across us and greeted us, then he said: Which of you is Muhammad? My companions went on and I stopped with him, and behold, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came in the middle of the army on a red camel, covering his head with his garment to protect him from the sun. I said: O questioner, this is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who has come to you. He said: Which of them is he? I said: The one with the red camel. He approached him and took hold of the reins of his camel, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, held him back and said: Are you Muhammad? He said: Yes. He said: I want to ask you about characteristics that no one on earth knows except one or two men. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ask whatever you want. He said: O Muhammad, does the Prophet sleep? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: His eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: O Muhammad, how does the child resemble his father and mother? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The man’s semen is white and thick, and the woman’s semen is yellow and thin. Which of the two semens prevails over the other, the child will be born? He said: You have spoken the truth. He asked: What does the man have from the child, and what does the woman have from it? He said: The man has the bones, veins, and nerves, and the woman has the flesh, blood, and hair. He said: You have spoken the truth. Then he said: O Muhammad, what is under this? - meaning the earth - The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Creation. He said: What is under them? He said: Earth. He said: What is under the earth? He said: Water. He said: What is under the water? He said: Darkness. He said: What is under the darkness? He said: Air. He said: What is under the air? He said: Soil. He said: What is under the soil? The eyes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, overflowed with tears, and he said: The knowledge of creation ends with the knowledge of the Creator. O questioner, the one asked about it does not know more than the questioner. He said: You have spoken the truth. I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, do you know who this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. This is what Gabriel, peace be upon him, said. This is a very strange hadith, and a strange context. Al-Qasim bin Abdul-Rahman is the only one who narrated it. Yahya bin Ma’in said about him: He is worth nothing. Abu Hatim al-Razi declared him weak, and Ibn ‘Adi said: He is not known. I said: He mixed up this hadith, and something entered into something else and a hadith into a hadith. It may be possible that he did that intentionally or that something entered into it, and God knows best. And His statement: “And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is more hidden.” That is, this Qur’an was sent down by the One who created the earth and the high heavens, the One who knows the secret and what is more hidden, as the Most High said: “Say, ‘He sent it down who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Ever-Forgiving, Most Merciful.’” Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He knows the secret and what is more hidden. He said: The secret is what the son of Adam keeps secret in himself. And what is more hidden is what was hidden from the son of Adam of what he will do before he knows it. So God knows all of that, so His knowledge of what has passed of that and what remains is one knowledge, and all of creation in that regard is like one soul with Him, and this is His statement: He did not create you and resurrect you except as one soul. Ad-Dahhak said: He knows the secret and what is more hidden. He said: The secret is what your soul speaks to, and what is more hidden is what your soul has not spoken to yet. Saeed bin Jubair said: You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you conceal tomorrow. God knows what you conceal today and what you conceal tomorrow. Mujahid said: And concealed means the whispering. He and Saeed bin Jubair also said: And concealed meaning what He knows of that which He did not speak to Himself. And His statement: “God, there is no god but He. To Him belong the best names” means the One who sent down the Qur’an to you. He is God, there is no god but He, the Possessor of the best names and the highest attributes. The hadiths that were narrated about the best names were presented at the end of Surat Al-A’raf. All praise and thanks be to God.
20:9: From here, the Blessed and Most High began to mention the story of Moses, and how the revelation to him began and he spoke to him, and that was after Moses had completed the term that was between him and his son-in-law in tending the sheep, and he traveled with his family, it was said: intending the land of Egypt after an absence from it of more than ten years, and with him his wife, so he lost his way and it was a winter night, and he stopped at a place between valleys and mountains in cold and winter and clouds and darkness and fog, and he began to strike a flint with him to kindle a fire as was his custom, but he did not strike anything and no sparks or anything came out of it, and while he was like that, he saw a fire from the side of the mountain, that is, a fire appeared to him from the side of the mountain that was there to his right, so he said to his family, giving them good report: Indeed, I have seen a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch from it, that is, a meteor of fire. In the other verse, or a burning ember from the fire, which is the ember with a flame, that you may warm yourselves, indicates the presence of cold. His saying: with a torch indicates the presence of darkness, and his saying: or I find on the fire a guide means someone who will guide me to the path, indicates that he has lost his way, as Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-A’war on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: or I find on the fire a guide he said: who will guide me to the path, and they were two sheep and they lost their way, so when he saw the fire he said: If I do not find anyone who will guide me to the path, I will bring you a fire to light.

20:11: God Almighty says: "So when he came to it meaning the fire, and approached it he was called, 'O Moses' and in another verse He was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot from the tree, 'O Moses, indeed I am God' and He said here Indeed, I am your Lord meaning the one who speaks to you and addresses you so take off your sandals" Ali bin Abi Talib, Abu Dharr, Abu Ayyub and more than one of the predecessors said: They were made of the skin of an unslaughtered donkey, and it was said: He was ordered to take off his sandals out of reverence for the spot. Saeed bin Jubair said: Just as a man is ordered to take off his sandals if he wants to enter the Kaaba, and it was said: So that he could tread the holy land with his feet barefoot and not wearing shoes, and other things were said, and God knows best. And his saying: "Tawa" Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is the name of the valley, and more than one said the same, so on this basis it is an explanatory apposition, and it was said: It is an expression of the command to tread with his feet, and it was said: Because it was sanctified twice, and the blessing was given to him and it was repeated, and the first is more correct like his saying: "When his Lord called to him in the sacred valley of Tawa". And his saying: "And I have chosen you" is like his saying: "Indeed, I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and My speech" meaning over all mankind who were present at his time, and it was said: God the Most High said: O Moses, do you know why I have singled you out for speaking from among mankind? He said: No, He said: Because no one has humbled himself before Me as you have. And his saying: "So listen to what is revealed meaning listen now to what I say to you and what I reveal to you Indeed, I am God, there is no god except Me" This is the first duty upon those who are accountable, to know that there is no god but God alone, with no partner. And His statement: Worship Me means, make Me One, and worship Me without any partner. And establish prayer for My remembrance. It was said that its meaning is, pray to remember Me. And it was said that its meaning is, And establish prayer when you remember Me. And what supports this second is what Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, al-Muthanna ibn Sa`id told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “If one of you sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, then let him pray it when he remembers it, for God the Most High said: And establish prayer for My remembrance.” And in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, its expiation is to pray it when he remembers it. There is no expiation for it other than that.” And His statement: The Hour is coming means it is inevitable and will happen. And his saying: "I almost conceal it" Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: "I almost conceal it from myself", meaning: because it is never concealed from God's Self. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "From Himself", and this is what Mujahid, Abu Salih and Yahya bin Rafi said. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "I almost conceal it", meaning: I do not inform anyone of it except myself. Al-Suddi said: There is no one from the people of the heavens and the earth except that God Almighty has concealed knowledge of the Hour from him, and in the recitation of Ibn Masoud it is: "I almost conceal it from myself", meaning: I concealed it from the creation until if I could conceal it from myself I would have done so. Qatada said: "I almost conceal it", and in some recitations it is: "I conceal it from myself", and by my life God has concealed it from the close angels and from the prophets and messengers. I said: This is like the saying of God Almighty: “Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except God.” And He said: “It is heavy in the heavens and the earth. It will not come to you except suddenly.” That is, its knowledge is heavy for the people of the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Munjab told us, Abu Numailah told us, Muhammad ibn Sahl al-Asadi told me on the authority of Waqqa’ who said: Sa’id ibn Jubayr recited it to me: I almost concealed it, meaning with the accusative of the alif and the genitive of the fa’, he said he revealed it, then he said: Have you not heard the saying of the poet: He worked for two months, then another month, like a doll with two couches hiding a deep well. Al-Suddi said: Al-Ghamir is a moist plant that grows in dry places, and Al-Arikin is a place, and Al-Damik is the perfect month, and this poem is by Ka’b bin Zuhair. And the words of God the Most High: That every soul may be rewarded for what it strives for means that I will establish it inevitably to reward every worker for his work. So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it “You will only be recompensed for what you used to do” and His words: So let not he who does not believe in it avert you from it the verse, what is meant by this address is the individuals who are accountable. That is, do not follow the path of those who deny the Hour, and turn to their pleasures in this world, and disobey their Lord and follow their desires, for whoever agrees with them in that has failed and lost, and will perish means will perish and be ruined. God the Most High said: And his wealth will not avail him when he falls.

Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Imam Malik: The hash is when a man places the stick on the branch and then moves it until its leaves and fruits fall without breaking the stick, so this is the hash and it does not beat. Scurrying means walking and shaking. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Abdah told us, Hafs ibn Juma’ told us, Samak told us on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent, scurrying about. He was called: O Moses, take it, but he did not take it. Then he was called a second time: Take it and do not fear. He was told the third time: You are among those who are secure, so he took it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said in his statement: So he threw it down, and behold, it was a serpent, darting about. He said: So he threw it down on the ground, then he looked and behold, it was a huge snake that the onlookers looked at, crawling as if it was seeking something that it wanted to take, passing by the rock like the back of a camel and swallowing it, and stabbing with one of its fangs at the base of the great tree and uprooting it, its eyes blazing with fire, and the spear had become like a crest from it, it was said: its hair is like meteors, and the two branches of it had become like a wide well in which there were molars and fangs that made a creaking sound. When Moses saw that, he turned and fled and did not look back. He went until he had gone deep and saw that he had defeated the serpent, then he remembered his Lord and stopped out of shyness before Him, then it was called, O Moses, return to where you were. So Moses returned, and he was very afraid, and he said: Take it with your right hand “and do not fear. We will restore it to its former state.” Moses was wearing a coat of wool at that time, so he entered it with a hook of sticks, and when he was ordered to take it, he lowered the end of the coat of mail over his hand, and said to him: King: Have you seen, O Moses, if God had permitted what you feared, would the armored cloak have availed you at all? He said: No, but I am weak, and from weakness I was created. So he uncovered his hand and placed it on the mouth of the snake until he heard the sound of the molars and fangs. Then he grasped it and behold, it was his staff that he had known, and behold, his hand was in the place where he used to place it when he leaned between the two branches. For this reason, God the Almighty said: We will restore it to its former state, meaning to the state it was known before that.

20:22: This is a second proof for Moses, peace be upon him, which is that God ordered him to put his hand in his pocket as He stated in the other verse, and here He expressed that by saying: And put your hand into your side and He said in another place: “And put your side into yourself from fear. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: By God, he brought it out as if it were a lamp, so Moses knew that he had met his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. Wahb said: His Lord said to him: Bring him closer, so he kept bringing him closer until he leaned his back against the trunk of the tree, so he settled down and the trembling went away from him. He put his hand on the staff and bowed his head and neck. And his saying: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed, meaning go to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, from whom you fled and escaped, and call him to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, and command him to be good to the Children of Israel and not to torture them, for he has transgressed and oppressed and preferred the life of this world and forgotten the Most High Lord. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God said to Moses: Go with My message, for you are in My hearing and My sight, and with you are My hands and My support, and I have clothed you with a paradise of My authority so that you may complete your strength in My command. You are a great army from among the army of My soldiers. I have sent you to a weak creation from among My creation who have become arrogant towards My blessings, and felt secure from My deception, and the world has deceived him from Me until he denied My right, and rejected My Lordship, and claimed that he did not know Me. I swear by My glory, were it not for the fate that I have placed between Me and My creation, I would have struck him with the strike of a tyrant who angers the heavens and the earth and the mountains and the seas. If I command the heavens, they will stone him, and if I command the earth, they will swallow him, and if I command the mountains, they will destroy him, and if I command the seas, they will drown him. But he has become insignificant to Me and has fallen from My sight, and My patience has encompassed him, and I have been satisfied with what I have and My right. Indeed, I am the Rich, and no one else is rich. So convey My message to him, and call him to My worship, and to My oneness and sincerity, and remind him of My days, and warn him of My vengeance and My punishment, and inform him that nothing can withstand My wrath. And say to him in between that a gentle word so that he may remember or fear, and tell him that I am quicker to pardon and forgiveness than I am to anger and punishment, and do not be alarmed by what I have clothed him with of the garments of this world, for his forelock is in my hand, and he does not speak, blink, or breathe except by my permission, and say to him: Answer your Lord, for He is the Most Forgiving, and He has given you respite for four hundred years, during all of which you are fighting Him, cursing Him, imitating Him, and turning His servants away from His path, and He sends rain from the sky upon you, and causes the earth to grow for you, and you will not become sick, nor grow old, nor become poor, nor be defeated, and if God had willed to hasten the punishment for you, He would have done so, but He is patient and forbearing, and strive against Him with yourself and your brother, and you both seek reward for your striving against Him, for if I had wanted to bring against him armies that he cannot withstand, I would have done so, but let this weak servant who has admired himself and his multitudes know that a small group, and not a small amount of Me, can overcome a large group by my permission, and do not be impressed by his adornments or what He has given you pleasure, and do not stretch your eyes toward that, for it is the flower of life. The world and the adornments of the luxurious, and if I wanted to adorn you from the world with adornments so that Pharaoh would know when he looked at it that his ability is incapable of what you have been given, I would have done so, but I desire you both from that and I turn it away from you, and thus I do with My friends, and it has been My custom in ancient times to do so, for I defend them from its pleasures and adornments as a compassionate shepherd defends his camels from the blessed burden, and that is not because they are insignificant to Me, but so that they may complete their portion in the abode of My honor, safe and prosperous, and the world has not spoken to them, and know that the servants do not adorn themselves for Me with adornments that are more eloquent than what I have of asceticism in the world, for it is the adornment of the righteous, upon them is a garment by which they are known from tranquility and humility, and their mark on their faces is from the traces of prostration, those are My friends truly truly, so when you meet them, lower your wing to them and humble your heart and tongue, and know that whoever humiliates a friend of Mine or frightens him has confronted Me with war and has begun to fight Me and has presented himself to Me and invited Me to it, and I am the quickest thing to aid My friends, so does the one who He fights me to stand up for me, or does he who opposes me think that he will defeat me, or does he who duels me think that he will outpace me or escape me, and how is it that I am the rebel for them in this world and the hereafter, and I do not dedicate their support to anyone other than myself? Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim: He said, ‘My Lord, expand for me my chest * And make my task easy for me.’ This is a question from Moses, peace be upon him, to his Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic, to expand his chest in what He sent him with, for He had commanded him with a great matter and a grave matter. He sent him to the greatest king on the face of the earth at that time, and the most tyrannical and most disbelieving of them, and the most numerous of them in soldiers, and the longest-lived of them in kingdom, and the most tyrannical and most rebellious of them. His affair reached the point that he claimed that he did not know God, and did not know of any god for his subjects other than Him. Moses remained in his house for a period as a child with them in the lap of Pharaoh on his bed, then he killed a person from them, and he feared that they would kill him, so he fled from them for this entire period, then after this his Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic, sent him to them as a warner calling them to God, the Almighty, the Majestic, that They worship Him alone, with no partner for Him. That is why He said: My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my task, meaning if You are not my helper, supporter, and backer, otherwise I have no power to do so. And untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech, because of the lisp that had afflicted him when the date and the coal were offered to him. He took the coal and placed it on his tongue, as will be explained. He did not ask for that to go away completely, but rather for the defect to go away and for them to understand what he wanted from him, which is as much as needed. If he had asked for everything, it would have gone away. However, the prophets do not ask except according to need, and that is why a remainder remained. God Almighty said, informing about Pharaoh, that he said: Or am I better than this one who is despised and can hardly articulate? That is, he speaks clearly. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: And untie the knot from my tongue. He said: Untie one knot. If he had asked for more than that, he would have been given. Ibn Abbas said: Moses complained to his Lord about what he feared from the people of Pharaoh regarding the one killed and the knot of his tongue, for there was a knot in his tongue that prevented him from speaking much, and he asked his Lord to help him with his brother Aaron to be a support for him and to speak on his behalf much of what his tongue could not express, so his request came to him and he untie the knot from his tongue. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Amr bin Othman, Baqiyah told us on the authority of Arta’ah bin Al-Mundhir, some of the companions of Muhammad bin Ka’b told me on his authority that he said: A relative of his came to him and said to him: There is nothing wrong with you except that you make mistakes in your speech and do not understand your recitation. Al-Qurazi said: O son of my brother, do I not understand you when I speak to you? He said: Yes. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, only asked his Lord to untie the knot from his tongue so that the Children of Israel would understand his speech, and he did not add anything to it. This is his wording. And his saying: And appoint for me a helper from my family, Aaron, my brother. This is also a question from Moses, peace be upon him, regarding a matter outside of him, which is the assistance of his brother Aaron to him. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Saeed on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Aaron was given a prophecy at that time when Moses, peace be upon them, was given a prophecy. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Numayr, Abu Usamah told us on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha that she went out while she was performing Umrah, and she stopped with some of the Bedouins, and she heard a man saying: Which brother was most beneficial to his brother in this world? They said: We do not know. He said: I swear by God I know. She said: So I said to myself in his oath, he does not exclude that he knows which brother was most beneficial to his brother in this world. He said: Moses when he asked for prophethood for his brother, so I said: By God, he spoke the truth. I said: And regarding this, God Almighty said in praise of Moses, peace be upon him: And he was honorable in the sight of God. And His statement: Strengthen my back with him Mujahid said: My back, And let him share in my task meaning in consulting me, so that we may glorify You much * and remember You much Mujahid said: The servant will not be among those who remember God much until he remembers God standing, sitting, and lying down. And His statement: Indeed, You have been Seeing of us meaning in Your choosing us and granting us prophethood, and sending us to Your enemy Pharaoh, so praise be to You for that.

Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Saeed on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Aaron was given a prophecy at that time when Moses, peace be upon them, was given a prophecy. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Numayr, Abu Usamah told us on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha that she went out while she was performing Umrah, and she stopped with some of the Bedouins, and she heard a man saying: Which brother was most beneficial to his brother in this world? They said: We do not know. He said: I swear by God I know. She said: So I said to myself in his oath, he does not exclude that he knows which brother was most beneficial to his brother in this world. He said: Moses when he asked for prophethood for his brother, so I said: By God, he spoke the truth. I said: And regarding this, God Almighty said in praise of Moses, peace be upon him: And he was honorable in the sight of God. And His statement: Strengthen my back with him Mujahid said: My back, And let him share in my task meaning in consulting me, so that we may glorify You much * and remember You much Mujahid said: The servant will not be among those who remember God much until he remembers God standing, sitting, and lying down. And His statement: Indeed, You have been Seeing of us meaning in Your choosing us and granting us prophethood, and sending us to Your enemy Pharaoh, so praise be to You for that.
20:36: This is an answer from God to His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, regarding what he asked of his Lord, the Almighty, and a reminder to him of His previous blessings upon him regarding what happened with his mother when she was breastfeeding him and warning him against Pharaoh and his people killing him, because he was born in the year in which they kill boys, so she made a coffin for him, and she was breastfeeding him and then putting him in it and sending him into the sea, which is the Nile, and holding him to her home with a rope, so she went once to tie the rope and it slipped from her and the sea took him, so she experienced the grief and worry that God mentioned about her in His saying: “And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty. She would have almost disclosed him had We not strengthened her heart.” So the sea took him to Pharaoh’s house. Then Pharaoh’s family picked him up to become for them an enemy and a grief, meaning a decree decreed by God, as they were killing the boys of the Children of Israel out of fear of Moses’ presence, so God decreed, and He has the great authority and complete power, that he would not be raised except on Pharaoh’s bed, and would be fed. With his food and drink, along with his wife’s love for him, and for this reason the Almighty said: An enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him, and I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning upon your enemy I made him love you. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: And I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning: I made you beloved to My servants. And that you may be brought up before My eyes, Abu Imran al-Jawni said: He was raised in the eye of God. Qatada said: He was fed before My eyes. Muammar ibn al-Muthanna said: And that you may be brought up before My eyes, so that I may see. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Meaning: I will make him live in the king’s house, enjoying himself and being pampered, and his food with them is the food of the king, so that is the craft. And His saying: “And when your sister walked and said: ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?’ So We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted.” That is because when he settled with the people of Pharaoh, they offered him wet nurses, but he refused. God Almighty said: And We had forbidden him wet nurses before. So his sister came and said: Shall I direct you to a family who will take care of him for you and be sincere to him? Meaning: Shall I direct you to someone who will breastfeed him for you for a fee? So she went with him and they were with her to his mother, and she offered him her breast, and he accepted it. They were very happy with that, and they hired her to breastfeed him, so she attained happiness, elevation, and comfort because of him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will be richer and more abundant. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith: The example of the craftsman who expects good in his craft is like the example of the mother of Moses who breastfeeds her son and takes her wages. And God Almighty said here: And We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted and she not grieve, meaning for you. And you killed a soul, meaning the Copt. And We saved you from distress, which is what happened to him because of his determination. Pharaoh's family wanted to kill him, so he fled from them until he reached the water of Madyan. That righteous man said to him: Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. And his saying: And We have tried you with trials. Imam Abu Abdul Rahman Ahmad bin Shuaib Al-Nasa’i, may God have mercy on him, said in the book of interpretation from his Sunan: His saying And We have tried you with trials Hadith of the trials: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Asbagh bin Zaid told us, Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me: I asked Abdullah bin Abbas about the saying of God Almighty to Moses, peace be upon him: And We have tried you with trials. So I asked him about the trials, what are they? He said: Start the day again, O Ibn Jubair, for they have a long story. So when morning came, I went to Ibn Abbas to complete what he promised me about the hadith of the trials. He said: Pharaoh and his companions were discussing what God had promised Abraham, peace be upon him, that He would make prophets and kings among his descendants. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are waiting for that and they have no doubt about it, and they thought that he was Joseph, son of Jacob. So when he died, they said: This is not how Abraham was promised, peace be upon him. So Pharaoh said: What do you think? So they plotted and agreed that he would send men with knives to go around among the Children of Israel and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. So they did that. When they saw that the adults of the Children of Israel were dying at their appointed times and the young were being slaughtered, they said: You are about to annihilate the Children of Israel and you will be at the point where you will be able to do the work and service that they used to do for you. So kill every male child one year and leave their daughters alone, and leave one year and do not kill any of them, so that the young will grow up in place of those who die from the adults. They will not increase in number because of those whom you are ashamed of, so that you will fear their increasing number with you, and they will not be destroyed because of those whom you kill and need. So they agreed on that. So Moses’ mother became pregnant with Aaron in the year in which boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. Then the following year, she became pregnant with Moses, peace be upon him, and worry and sadness fell into her heart. That is from the trials - O Ibn Jubayr - that which came upon him while he was in his mother’s womb, which is intended. Then God revealed to her, "Do not fear and do not grieve. We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers." So He commanded her, when she gave birth, to put him in a coffin and then throw him into the sea. So when she gave birth, she did that. Then, when her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her and she said to herself, What have you done with my son? If he were slaughtered here and I buried him and shrouded him, that would be more beloved to me than to throw him to the beasts and whales of the sea. The water reached him until it reached the watering place of the maids of Pharaoh's wife. When they saw him, they seized him and wanted to open the chest. Some of them said: There is money in this, and if we open it, the king's wife will not believe us with what we found in it. So they carried it as it was and did not take anything out of it until they gave it to her. When she opened it, she saw a boy in it, and God bestowed upon him a love from her that He had never bestowed upon anyone before. The heart of Moses' mother became empty of remembering everything except the mention of Moses. When the slaughterers heard of his command, they came with their knives to Pharaoh's wife to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. She said to them: Leave him alone, for this one will not increase the number of the Children of Israel until I go to Pharaoh and ask him for his gift. If he gives him to me, you will have done well and acted well, but if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you. So she went to Pharaoh and said: A delight to me and you. Pharaoh said: He will be for you, but as for me, I have no need of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And by Him he swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be the comfort of his eye as his wife had acknowledged, God would have guided him as he had guided her, but He deprived him of that. So she sent to those around her, to every woman who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him. But whenever one of them took him to breastfeed him, he would not accept her breast until Pharaoh’s wife feared that he would refuse milk and die. That saddened her, so she ordered him to be taken out to the market and the assembly of people, hoping that she would find a wet nurse for him to take from her, but he did not accept. Moses' mother became obsessed and said to his sister: "Follow him and look for him. Do you hear him say, 'Is my son alive or has the beasts eaten him?'" She forgot what God had promised her. His sister saw him from afar, and they were unaware. Afar is when a person's eyes look at something far away, but it is beside him, and he is unaware of it. So she said out of joy when the wet nurses were exhausted: I will show you a household that will take care of him for you and will be sincere to him. So they took her and said, How do you know that they were sincere to him? Do they know him? Until they doubted that, and that is from the temptations, O Ibn Jubayr. So she said: Their advice to him and their compassion for him, their desire for the king’s wet nurse and the hope of the king’s benefit, so they left her. So she went to her mother and told her the report. So his mother came and when she placed him in her lap, he climbed onto her breast and sucked it until his sides were filled with moisture. And the good report went to Pharaoh’s wife to give her the good report that we have found a wet nurse for your son. So she sent to her and brought her and him. When she saw what was being done to her, she said: Stay and nurse this son of mine, for I have never loved anything as much as he has loved. Moses' mother said: I cannot leave my house and my son to be lost. If you are willing to give him to me, I will take him to my house and he will be with me. I will spare no good for him, for I will not leave my house and my son. Moses' mother remembered what God had promised her, and she felt sorry for Pharaoh's wife and was certain that God would fulfill His promise. She returned with him to her house that day, and God made him grow well and preserved him for what He had decreed for him. The children of Israel, who were in the outskirts of the village, remained free from the oppression and injustice that was among them. When he grew up, Pharaoh’s wife said to Moses’ mother: Will you show me my son? So she called her for a day in which she could show him to her. Pharaoh’s wife said to her keepers, wet nurses, and maidservants: “Let not one of you remain without receiving my son today with a gift and honor so that I may see that. I am sending a trustee to record what each one of you does.” So gifts, honor, and gifts continued to greet him from the time he left his mother’s house until he entered upon Pharaoh’s wife. When he entered upon her, she honored him and was pleased with him, and his mother bestowed gifts because of her good influence on him. Then she said: Let us bring him to Pharaoh so that he may bestow gifts upon him and honor him. So when she entered upon him, he placed him in his lap. Moses took Pharaoh’s beard and stretched it to the ground. Then the seducers from among the enemies of God said to Pharaoh: “Do you not see what God promised His prophet Abraham? He claimed that he would inherit you, rise above you, and defeat you. So he sent for the slaughterers to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr after every calamity he was afflicted with. And he wanted to cause trials, so Pharaoh's wife came and said: What do you want with this boy whom you gave me? He said: Do you not see that he claims that he can wrestle with me and be superior to me? She said: Make a matter between me and you by which the truth will be known. Bring two live coals and two pearls and present them to him. If he grabs the two pearls and avoids the live coals, you will know that he is sane. But if he takes the live coals and does not want the pearls, you will know that no one would prefer the live coals to the pearls while he is sane. So the live coals and the pearls were brought to him, and he took the live coals and snatched them away from him for fear that they would burn his hand. The woman said: Do you not see? Then God turned him away from him after he had intended to do it, and God accomplished His command with him, and when he reached his full maturity and was a man, no one from the family of Pharaoh would get to any of the Children of Israel with him by oppression or force, until they refused completely. While Moses, peace be upon him, was walking in the direction of the city, he saw two men fighting, one of them a Pharaoh and the other an Israelite. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, and Moses became very angry, because he attacked him while he knew his status among the Children of Israel and his protection of them, and no one knew except that it was from breastfeeding except Moses’ mother, unless God informed Moses of that which no one else knew. So Moses struck the Pharaoh and killed him, and no one saw them except God, the Almighty, and the Israelite. Moses said when he killed the man: This is from the work of Satan, he is a clear, misleading enemy. Then he said: “My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.” So He forgave him, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. So he stayed in the city, afraid, waiting for report. Then he came to Pharaoh and it was said to him: The Children of Israel killed a man from the family of Pharaoh, so take our right for us and do not give them concessions. He said: Find me his killer and someone who can testify against him, for the king, even if he is on good terms with his people, cannot be bound without evidence or proof. So seek knowledge of that for me and I will take your right for you. While they were wandering around and finding no proof, Moses saw the next day that Israelite fighting a man from the family of another Pharaoh. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, but he came across Moses and regretted what he had done and hated what he had seen. The Israelite became angry and wanted to strike the Pharaoh. So he said to the Israelite for what he had done yesterday and today: You are clearly a liar. The Israelite looked at Moses after he had said what he had said to him, and he was as angry as he had been the day before when he had killed the Pharaoh. He feared that after he had said to him that you are a clear liar, he had meant him and had not meant him, but rather he meant the Pharaoh. The Israelite became afraid and said: O Moses, do you want to He said this out of fear that Moses wanted to kill him. So they parted ways and the Pharaoh went and told them what he had heard from the Israelite when he said: O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? So Fu’un sent the slaughterers to kill Moses. So the messengers of Pharaoh took the main road, walking at their own pace, seeking Moses, not fearing that they would miss him. Then a man from Moses’ party came from the farthest part of the city, and he took a shortcut until he reached Moses before them and told him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. Moses set out towards Madyan, and he had not encountered any calamity before that, and he had no knowledge of the road except his good opinion of his Lord, the Almighty, for he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way. And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their flocks, and he found besides them two women holding back their sheep. So he said to them: What is the matter with you, that you are isolated and not watering your flocks with the people? They said: We do not have the strength to compete with the people, but we drink from the excess of their watering place. So he watered for them and began to scoop up a lot of water in the bucket until he was the first of the shepherds. Then they returned with their sheep to their father, and Moses, peace be upon him, returned and took shelter under a tree and said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need. Their father was surprised at their quick return with their sheep, full and content, so he said: You have a matter today. So they told him what Moses had done. So he ordered one of them to call him, so she went to Moses and called him. When he spoke to him, he said: “Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom.” One of them said: “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.” So jealousy made him say to her: How do you know what his strength is or how trustworthy he is? She said: As for his strength, I did not see him in the bucket when he watered for us. I have never seen a man stronger in that watering than him. As for his trustworthiness, he looked at me when I came to him and looked at him, and when he knew that I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it until I delivered your message to him. Then he said to me: Walk behind me and describe the way to me. He did this only because he is trustworthy. So her father was pleased and believed her and thought of him what she said. So he said to him: Would you like me to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you hire me for eight years. If you complete ten, it will be from you. I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous? So he did so. Eight years were obligatory for the Prophet of God, Moses, and two years were his waiting period. So God fulfilled his waiting period and he completed it to ten. Saeed, who is Ibn Jubayr, said: A Christian scholar met me and said: Do you know which of the two terms Moses fulfilled? I said: No, and I did not know at that time. So I met Ibn Abbas and mentioned that to him, and he said: Did you not know that eight were obligatory upon the Prophet of God, and the Prophet of God would not decrease anything from them, and he knows that God was fulfilling the promise that He had made for Moses, for he fulfilled ten years. So I met the Christian and told him that, and he said: The one whom you asked and he informed you knows more about that than you. I said: Yes, and more appropriate. So when Moses set out with his family, there was something about the fire, the staff, and his hand that God has told you about in the Qur’an. So he complained to God Almighty about what he feared from the family of Pharaoh regarding the one killed and the knot of his tongue, for there was a knot in his tongue that prevented him from speaking much, and he asked his Lord to help him with his brother Aaron to be a support for him and to speak on his behalf much of what his tongue could not express. So God granted him his request and loosened the knot from his tongue, and God inspired Aaron and commanded him to meet him, so Moses rushed with his staff until he met Aaron, peace be upon them, and they both went to Pharaoh, and they stayed on His door was closed for a while, but they were not given permission. Then he gave them permission after a severe veil. They said: We are messengers of your Lord. He said: Who is your Lord? So tell him what God has told you in the Qur’an. He said: What do you want? The dead man mentioned to him and apologized for what he had heard. He said: I want you to believe in God and send the Children of Israel with us. But he refused and said: Bring a sign if you are of the truthful. So he threw down his staff and behold, it was a great, darting serpent, opening its mouth, rushing toward Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw it heading toward him, he was afraid of it and rushed from his bed and called upon Moses to stop it from him, and he did so. Then he took his hand out of his pocket and saw it white without any defect, meaning without leprosy. Then he put it back and it returned to its original color. So he consulted the nobles around him about what he had seen, and they said to him: These are two magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic and do away with your best way, meaning their kingdom that they were in and their livelihood. And they refused to give Moses anything of what he asked for, and they said to him: Gather for them the magicians, for there are many in your land until you overcome their magic with your magic. So he sent to the cities and gathered for him every learned magician. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: What does this magician do? They said: He works with snakes. They said: By God, no one on earth works magic with snakes, ropes and sticks as we do. So what is our reward if we are defeated? He said to them: You are my relatives and my special ones, and I will do for you whatever you like. So they made an appointment on the Day of Adornment and that the people would be gathered at noon. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ibn Abbas told me that the day of adornment was the day on which God gave victory to Moses over Pharaoh and the magicians, which was the day of Ashura. So when they gathered in one place, the people said to one another: Go, let us attend to this matter. Perhaps we will follow the magicians, if they are the ones who are victorious, meaning Moses and Aaron, mocking them. They said, O Moses, either you throw or we will be the ones to throw. He said, Throw. “So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, ‘By the might of Pharaoh, we will surely be the victors.’” Moses saw from their magic what made him fear, so God inspired him to throw down his staff. When he threw it down, it became a huge serpent with its mouth open. The staffs began to entangle themselves with the ropes until they became islands that the serpent entered into until it did not leave a single staff or rope without devouring it. When the magicians realized that, they said, “If this were magic, our magic would not have reached all this, but this is a command from God Almighty. We believe in God and in what Moses brought from God, and we repent to God for what we were doing.” So God broke the back of Pharaoh and his followers in that place, and the truth appeared and what they were doing was nullified. So they were defeated there and returned humiliated. Pharaoh’s wife was prominent and disheveled, calling on God for victory for Moses over Pharaoh and his followers. Whoever from Pharaoh’s family saw her thought that she was only She was humbled to pity Pharaoh and his followers, but her sorrow and concern were for Moses. When Moses remained with Pharaoh’s false promises for a long time, whenever he brought a sign, he promised her that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But when it passed, he broke his promise and said: Can your Lord do anything other than this? So God sent upon his people the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, detailed signs. All of them complained to Moses and asked him to stop them from him and to covenant with him to send the Children of Israel with him. If he stopped them from him, he broke his promise and violated his covenant until God ordered Moses to go out with his people. He went out with them at night. When Pharaoh woke up and saw that they had gone, he sent gatherers to the cities, and he followed him with many great armies. God revealed to the sea, When My servant Moses strikes you with his staff, and it split into twelve divisions until Moses and those with him crossed. Then it converged on those who remained after that from Pharaoh and his followers. Moses forgot to strike the sea with the staff and ended up at the sea, and it had a raging crust, fearing that Moses would strike it with his staff while he was unaware, and he would become disobedient to God. So when the two hosts saw each other and came close together, the companions of Moses said, "We are surely to be overtaken. Do what your Lord has commanded you, for indeed, He has not lied, and you have not lied." He said, My Lord has promised me that when I come to the sea, it will split into twelve divisions so that I may cross it. Then after that he mentioned the staff, so he struck the sea with his staff when the first of Pharaoh's army drew near the last of Moses' army, and the sea split as his Lord had commanded him and as He had promised Moses. When Moses and all his companions had crossed the sea and Pharaoh and his companions had entered, the sea met them as he had been commanded. When Moses had crossed the sea, his companions said, Indeed, we fear that Pharaoh has drowned, and we do not believe in his perishing. So he called upon his Lord, who brought him out for him in his body until they were certain of his perishing. Then after that they passed by a people who were devoted to their idols. "They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. * Indeed, what they are in is ruined.'" You have seen and heard what suffices you. Then he went and Moses settled them in a place and said, "Obey Aaron, for I have made him your successor. I am going to my Lord." And he gave them a respite of thirty days in which he would return to them. So when he came to his Lord and wanted to speak to Him during the thirty days, he had fasted day and night, and he hated to speak to his Lord while the odor of one who is fasting smelled from him. So Moses took some vegetation from the ground and chewed it. Then his Lord said to him when he came to Him, Why have you broken your fast? And He is most knowing of what happened. He said, O Lord, I hated to speak to You except while my mouth smelled good. He said, Did you not know, O Moses, that the odor of one who is fasting is better to Me than the odor of musk? Go back and fast ten days, then come to Me. So Moses, peace be upon him, did what he was ordered to do. When his people saw that he did not return to them within the appointed time, they were upset. Aaron had addressed them and said: You have left Egypt, and Pharaoh’s people have loans and deposits with you, and you have the same with them. I see that you are counting what you have with them, and I do not permit for you a deposit that you have entrusted to you or a loan. We will not return anything of that to them, nor will we keep it for ourselves. So he dug a hole and ordered every people who had any of that, whether it was a commodity or an ornament, to throw it into that hole. Then he lit a fire over it and burned it. He said: It will not be for us or for them. The Samaritan was from a people who worshipped cows, neighbors of the Children of Israel, but he was not from the Children of Israel. So he was carried with Moses and the Children of Israel when they were carried. It was decreed that he saw a trace and took a handful of it. He passed by Aaron, and Aaron, peace be upon him, said to him: O Samaritan, will you not throw away what is in your hand, while he is holding it and no one sees it during that time? He said: This is a handful of the trace of the Messenger who crossed the sea with you, and I will not throw it for anything except that you pray to God when you throw it to make it what I want. So he threw it and Aaron prayed for him, and he said: I want it to be a calf. So everything that was in the pit of goods or ornaments or copper or iron gathered together and it became a hollow calf with no soul in it and it mooed. Ibn Abbas said: No, by God, it never had a voice. Rather, the wind entered its anus and came out of its mouth, and that sound was from that. So the Children of Israel split into groups, and a group said: O Samaritan, what is this and you know best about it? He said: This is your Lord, but Moses has lost his way. A group said: We will not deny this until Moses returns to us. If he is our Lord, we would not have lost him and failed in his cause when we saw him. If he is not our Lord, then we will follow the words of Moses. A group said: This is the work of Satan, and he is not our Lord, and we do not believe in him or believe him. A group imbibed the truth in their hearts with what the Samaritan said about the calf, and they declared their denial of it. Then Aaron said to them: O my people, you are only being tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command. They said: So what is the matter with Moses, that he promised us thirty days and then broke his promise? These forty days have passed. Their fools said: His Lord has made a mistake, so he is seeking him: following him. When God spoke to Moses and told him what He said, He informed him of what his people had encountered after him. So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, and he said to them what you have heard in the Qur’an. He took hold of his brother’s head, dragging him towards him, and threw down the tablets in anger. Then he excused his brother with his excuse and asked forgiveness for him, and went back to the Samaritan. He said to him: What made you do what you did? He said: I took a handful of the Messenger’s trace and understood it, but you were blind to it. “So I cast it aside, and thus my soul enticed me. He said: Then go, for in this life you will have the right to say, ‘No contact,’ and you have an appointment which you will not fail to fulfill. And look to your god, to whom you have been devoted. We will surely burn him and scatter him into the sea as a blast.” Had he been a god, he would not have achieved that from him. The Children of Israel were certain of the trial, and those who had the same opinion of him as Aaron rejoiced, so they said to their group: O Moses, ask your Lord to open for us a door of repentance that we may do, and He will forgive us for what we have done. So Moses chose from his people seventy men who would spare no effort in doing good, the best of the Children of Israel and those who had not associated partners with God in the calf. He set out with them asking for their repentance, and the earth shook under them! The Prophet of God felt ashamed before his people and his delegation when he did to them what he did, so he said: “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done?” Among them were those whom God had seen of the love of the calf and their belief in it that had permeated their hearts, and for that reason the earth shook with them. He said: “And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses - those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written down in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel.” So he said: “O Lord, I asked You for repentance for my people, and You said that My mercy was written for a people other than my people. Why did You not delay me until You bring me out into the nation of that man who has been shown mercy?” He said to him: Their repentance is that each man among them kills whoever he meets of father and son, killing him with the sword and not caring who he kills in that place. Those who were hidden from Moses and Aaron repented, and God saw their sins, so they confessed to them and did what they were commanded, and God forgave the killer and the one killed. Then Moses, peace be upon him, walked with them towards the Holy Land, and took the tablets after his anger subsided, and ordered them to do what he ordered them to do of the duties, but that was heavy on them and they refused to acknowledge it, so God made the mountain appear to them as if it were a canopy and approached them until they feared it would fall on them, so they took the book in their right hands while they were listening, looking at the mountain and the book in their hands while they were behind the mountain for fear that it would fall on them, then they went until they came to the Holy Land and found a city in which there were tyrannical people, their creation was strange, and they mentioned from their fruits something amazing about its size, so they said: O Moses, there are tyrannical people in it that we cannot bear, and we will not enter it as long as they are in it, but if they leave it, then we will enter. Two men from those who feared said: It was said to Yazid: Did he read it like this? He said: Yes, from the tyrants we believed in Moses and they went out to him and said: We know our people best. If you only fear what you have seen of their bodies and their numbers, then they have no hearts and no strength, so enter upon them through the gate, and when you enter it, you will be victorious. And some people say: They are from the people of Moses. So those who feared from the Children of Israel said: They said: O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here. So they angered Moses, so he invoked against them and called them wicked, and he had not invoked against them before that when he saw their disobedience and their wrongdoing until that day, so God answered him and called them as Moses had called them wicked, and forbade them from it for forty years, wandering in the land, waking up every day and walking, with no resting place. And He shaded them with clouds in the wilderness, and sent down upon them manna and quails, and made for them clothes that would not wear out or get dirty, and He placed a square stone among them, and commanded Moses to strike it. With his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from it, three springs in each direction, and he informed each tribe of the spring from which they would drink, and they would not move from one place except that they would find that stone among them in the place where it had been the day before. Ibn Abbas traced this hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I believe that Muawiyah heard Ibn Abbas narrating this hadith and he denied that the Pharaoh was the one who disclosed to Moses the matter of the one killed. He said: How could he disclose it to him when he had no knowledge of it and no one was present at it except the Israelite who was present?
