Ibn Abbas became angry and took Muawiyah by the hand and went with him to Sa`d ibn Malik al-Zuhri and said to him: O Abu Ishaq, do you remember the day when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us about the one killed by Moses from the family of Pharaoh? Was it the Israelite who disclosed it or the Pharaoh? He said: The Pharaoh only revealed to him what he heard from the Israelite who witnessed and was present at that. This is how al-Nasa’i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim included it in their interpretations, all of them from the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun with it, and it is attributed to Ibn Abbas, and there is nothing in it that is attributed to the Prophet except a little of it, and it seems that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, received it from what was permitted to be transmitted from the Israelite narrations from Ka’b al-Ahbar, or someone else, and God knows best. I heard our Sheikh, the preserver Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, say that as well. And the Almighty said:
20:37: This is an answer from God to His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, regarding what he asked of his Lord, the Almighty, and a reminder to him of His previous blessings upon him regarding what happened with his mother when she was breastfeeding him and warning him against Pharaoh and his people killing him, because he was born in the year in which they kill boys, so she made a coffin for him, and she was breastfeeding him and then putting him in it and sending him into the sea, which is the Nile, and holding him to her home with a rope, so she went once to tie the rope and it slipped from her and the sea took him, so she experienced the grief and worry that God mentioned about her in His saying: “And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty. She would have almost disclosed him had We not strengthened her heart.” So the sea took him to Pharaoh’s house. Then Pharaoh’s family picked him up to become for them an enemy and a grief, meaning a decree decreed by God, as they were killing the boys of the Children of Israel out of fear of Moses’ presence, so God decreed, and He has the great authority and complete power, that he would not be raised except on Pharaoh’s bed, and would be fed. With his food and drink, along with his wife’s love for him, and for this reason the Almighty said: An enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him, and I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning upon your enemy I made him love you. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: And I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning: I made you beloved to My servants. And that you may be brought up before My eyes, Abu Imran al-Jawni said: He was raised in the eye of God. Qatada said: He was fed before My eyes. Muammar ibn al-Muthanna said: And that you may be brought up before My eyes, so that I may see. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Meaning: I will make him live in the king’s house, enjoying himself and being pampered, and his food with them is the food of the king, so that is the craft. And His saying: “And when your sister walked and said: ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?’ So We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted.” That is because when he settled with the people of Pharaoh, they offered him wet nurses, but he refused. God Almighty said: And We had forbidden him wet nurses before. So his sister came and said: Shall I direct you to a family who will take care of him for you and be sincere to him? Meaning: Shall I direct you to someone who will breastfeed him for you for a fee? So she went with him and they were with her to his mother, and she offered him her breast, and he accepted it. They were very happy with that, and they hired her to breastfeed him, so she attained happiness, elevation, and comfort because of him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will be richer and more abundant. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith: The example of the craftsman who expects good in his craft is like the example of the mother of Moses who breastfeeds her son and takes her wages. And God Almighty said here: And We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted and she not grieve, meaning for you. And you killed a soul, meaning the Copt. And We saved you from distress, which is what happened to him because of his determination. Pharaoh's family wanted to kill him, so he fled from them until he reached the water of Madyan. That righteous man said to him: Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. And his saying: And We have tried you with trials. Imam Abu Abdul Rahman Ahmad bin Shuaib Al-Nasa’i, may God have mercy on him, said in the book of interpretation from his Sunan: His saying And We have tried you with trials Hadith of the trials: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Asbagh bin Zaid told us, Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me: I asked Abdullah bin Abbas about the saying of God Almighty to Moses, peace be upon him: And We have tried you with trials. So I asked him about the trials, what are they? He said: Start the day again, O Ibn Jubair, for they have a long story. So when morning came, I went to Ibn Abbas to complete what he promised me about the hadith of the trials. He said: Pharaoh and his companions were discussing what God had promised Abraham, peace be upon him, that He would make prophets and kings among his descendants. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are waiting for that and they have no doubt about it, and they thought that he was Joseph, son of Jacob. So when he died, they said: This is not how Abraham was promised, peace be upon him. So Pharaoh said: What do you think? So they plotted and agreed that he would send men with knives to go around among the Children of Israel and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. So they did that. When they saw that the adults of the Children of Israel were dying at their appointed times and the young were being slaughtered, they said: You are about to annihilate the Children of Israel and you will be at the point where you will be able to do the work and service that they used to do for you. So kill every male child one year and leave their daughters alone, and leave one year and do not kill any of them, so that the young will grow up in place of those who die from the adults. They will not increase in number because of those whom you are ashamed of, so that you will fear their increasing number with you, and they will not be destroyed because of those whom you kill and need. So they agreed on that. So Moses’ mother became pregnant with Aaron in the year in which boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. Then the following year, she became pregnant with Moses, peace be upon him, and worry and sadness fell into her heart. That is from the trials - O Ibn Jubayr - that which came upon him while he was in his mother’s womb, which is intended. Then God revealed to her, "Do not fear and do not grieve. We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers." So He commanded her, when she gave birth, to put him in a coffin and then throw him into the sea. So when she gave birth, she did that. Then, when her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her and she said to herself, What have you done with my son? If he were slaughtered here and I buried him and shrouded him, that would be more beloved to me than to throw him to the beasts and whales of the sea. The water reached him until it reached the watering place of the maids of Pharaoh's wife. When they saw him, they seized him and wanted to open the chest. Some of them said: There is money in this, and if we open it, the king's wife will not believe us with what we found in it. So they carried it as it was and did not take anything out of it until they gave it to her. When she opened it, she saw a boy in it, and God bestowed upon him a love from her that He had never bestowed upon anyone before. The heart of Moses' mother became empty of remembering everything except the mention of Moses. When the slaughterers heard of his command, they came with their knives to Pharaoh's wife to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. She said to them: Leave him alone, for this one will not increase the number of the Children of Israel until I go to Pharaoh and ask him for his gift. If he gives him to me, you will have done well and acted well, but if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you. So she went to Pharaoh and said: A delight to me and you. Pharaoh said: He will be for you, but as for me, I have no need of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And by Him he swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be the comfort of his eye as his wife had acknowledged, God would have guided him as he had guided her, but He deprived him of that. So she sent to those around her, to every woman who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him. But whenever one of them took him to breastfeed him, he would not accept her breast until Pharaoh’s wife feared that he would refuse milk and die. That saddened her, so she ordered him to be taken out to the market and the assembly of people, hoping that she would find a wet nurse for him to take from her, but he did not accept. Moses' mother became obsessed and said to his sister: "Follow him and look for him. Do you hear him say, 'Is my son alive or has the beasts eaten him?'" She forgot what God had promised her. His sister saw him from afar, and they were unaware. Afar is when a person's eyes look at something far away, but it is beside him, and he is unaware of it. So she said out of joy when the wet nurses were exhausted: I will show you a household that will take care of him for you and will be sincere to him. So they took her and said, How do you know that they were sincere to him? Do they know him? Until they doubted that, and that is from the temptations, O Ibn Jubayr. So she said: Their advice to him and their compassion for him, their desire for the king’s wet nurse and the hope of the king’s benefit, so they left her. So she went to her mother and told her the report. So his mother came and when she placed him in her lap, he climbed onto her breast and sucked it until his sides were filled with moisture. And the good report went to Pharaoh’s wife to give her the good report that we have found a wet nurse for your son. So she sent to her and brought her and him. When she saw what was being done to her, she said: Stay and nurse this son of mine, for I have never loved anything as much as he has loved. Moses' mother said: I cannot leave my house and my son to be lost. If you are willing to give him to me, I will take him to my house and he will be with me. I will spare no good for him, for I will not leave my house and my son. Moses' mother remembered what God had promised her, and she felt sorry for Pharaoh's wife and was certain that God would fulfill His promise. She returned with him to her house that day, and God made him grow well and preserved him for what He had decreed for him. The children of Israel, who were in the outskirts of the village, remained free from the oppression and injustice that was among them. When he grew up, Pharaoh’s wife said to Moses’ mother: Will you show me my son? So she called her for a day in which she could show him to her. Pharaoh’s wife said to her keepers, wet nurses, and maidservants: “Let not one of you remain without receiving my son today with a gift and honor so that I may see that. I am sending a trustee to record what each one of you does.” So gifts, honor, and gifts continued to greet him from the time he left his mother’s house until he entered upon Pharaoh’s wife. When he entered upon her, she honored him and was pleased with him, and his mother bestowed gifts because of her good influence on him. Then she said: Let us bring him to Pharaoh so that he may bestow gifts upon him and honor him. So when she entered upon him, he placed him in his lap. Moses took Pharaoh’s beard and stretched it to the ground. Then the seducers from among the enemies of God said to Pharaoh: “Do you not see what God promised His prophet Abraham? He claimed that he would inherit you, rise above you, and defeat you. So he sent for the slaughterers to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr after every calamity he was afflicted with. And he wanted to cause trials, so Pharaoh's wife came and said: What do you want with this boy whom you gave me? He said: Do you not see that he claims that he can wrestle with me and be superior to me? She said: Make a matter between me and you by which the truth will be known. Bring two live coals and two pearls and present them to him. If he grabs the two pearls and avoids the live coals, you will know that he is sane. But if he takes the live coals and does not want the pearls, you will know that no one would prefer the live coals to the pearls while he is sane. So the live coals and the pearls were brought to him, and he took the live coals and snatched them away from him for fear that they would burn his hand. The woman said: Do you not see? Then God turned him away from him after he had intended to do it, and God accomplished His command with him, and when he reached his full maturity and was a man, no one from the family of Pharaoh would get to any of the Children of Israel with him by oppression or force, until they refused completely. While Moses, peace be upon him, was walking in the direction of the city, he saw two men fighting, one of them a Pharaoh and the other an Israelite. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, and Moses became very angry, because he attacked him while he knew his status among the Children of Israel and his protection of them, and no one knew except that it was from breastfeeding except Moses’ mother, unless God informed Moses of that which no one else knew. So Moses struck the Pharaoh and killed him, and no one saw them except God, the Almighty, and the Israelite. Moses said when he killed the man: This is from the work of Satan, he is a clear, misleading enemy. Then he said: “My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.” So He forgave him, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. So he stayed in the city, afraid, waiting for report. Then he came to Pharaoh and it was said to him: The Children of Israel killed a man from the family of Pharaoh, so take our right for us and do not give them concessions. He said: Find me his killer and someone who can testify against him, for the king, even if he is on good terms with his people, cannot be bound without evidence or proof. So seek knowledge of that for me and I will take your right for you. While they were wandering around and finding no proof, Moses saw the next day that Israelite fighting a man from the family of another Pharaoh. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, but he came across Moses and regretted what he had done and hated what he had seen. The Israelite became angry and wanted to strike the Pharaoh. So he said to the Israelite for what he had done yesterday and today: You are clearly a liar. The Israelite looked at Moses after he had said what he had said to him, and he was as angry as he had been the day before when he had killed the Pharaoh. He feared that after he had said to him that you are a clear liar, he had meant him and had not meant him, but rather he meant the Pharaoh. The Israelite became afraid and said: O Moses, do you want to He said this out of fear that Moses wanted to kill him. So they parted ways and the Pharaoh went and told them what he had heard from the Israelite when he said: O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? So Fu’un sent the slaughterers to kill Moses. So the messengers of Pharaoh took the main road, walking at their own pace, seeking Moses, not fearing that they would miss him. Then a man from Moses’ party came from the farthest part of the city, and he took a shortcut until he reached Moses before them and told him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. Moses set out towards Madyan, and he had not encountered any calamity before that, and he had no knowledge of the road except his good opinion of his Lord, the Almighty, for he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way. And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their flocks, and he found besides them two women holding back their sheep. So he said to them: What is the matter with you, that you are isolated and not watering your flocks with the people? They said: We do not have the strength to compete with the people, but we drink from the excess of their watering place. So he watered for them and began to scoop up a lot of water in the bucket until he was the first of the shepherds. Then they returned with their sheep to their father, and Moses, peace be upon him, returned and took shelter under a tree and said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need. Their father was surprised at their quick return with their sheep, full and content, so he said: You have a matter today. So they told him what Moses had done. So he ordered one of them to call him, so she went to Moses and called him. When he spoke to him, he said: “Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom.” One of them said: “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.” So jealousy made him say to her: How do you know what his strength is or how trustworthy he is? She said: As for his strength, I did not see him in the bucket when he watered for us. I have never seen a man stronger in that watering than him. As for his trustworthiness, he looked at me when I came to him and looked at him, and when he knew that I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it until I delivered your message to him. Then he said to me: Walk behind me and describe the way to me. He did this only because he is trustworthy. So her father was pleased and believed her and thought of him what she said. So he said to him: Would you like me to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you hire me for eight years. If you complete ten, it will be from you. I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous? So he did so. Eight years were obligatory for the Prophet of God, Moses, and two years were his waiting period. So God fulfilled his waiting period and he completed it to ten. Saeed, who is Ibn Jubayr, said: A Christian scholar met me and said: Do you know which of the two terms Moses fulfilled? I said: No, and I did not know at that time. So I met Ibn Abbas and mentioned that to him, and he said: Did you not know that eight were obligatory upon the Prophet of God, and the Prophet of God would not decrease anything from them, and he knows that God was fulfilling the promise that He had made for Moses, for he fulfilled ten years. So I met the Christian and told him that, and he said: The one whom you asked and he informed you knows more about that than you. I said: Yes, and more appropriate. So when Moses set out with his family, there was something about the fire, the staff, and his hand that God has told you about in the Qur’an. So he complained to God Almighty about what he feared from the family of Pharaoh regarding the one killed and the knot of his tongue, for there was a knot in his tongue that prevented him from speaking much, and he asked his Lord to help him with his brother Aaron to be a support for him and to speak on his behalf much of what his tongue could not express. So God granted him his request and loosened the knot from his tongue, and God inspired Aaron and commanded him to meet him, so Moses rushed with his staff until he met Aaron, peace be upon them, and they both went to Pharaoh, and they stayed on His door was closed for a while, but they were not given permission. Then he gave them permission after a severe veil. They said: We are messengers of your Lord. He said: Who is your Lord? So tell him what God has told you in the Qur’an. He said: What do you want? The dead man mentioned to him and apologized for what he had heard. He said: I want you to believe in God and send the Children of Israel with us. But he refused and said: Bring a sign if you are of the truthful. So he threw down his staff and behold, it was a great, darting serpent, opening its mouth, rushing toward Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw it heading toward him, he was afraid of it and rushed from his bed and called upon Moses to stop it from him, and he did so. Then he took his hand out of his pocket and saw it white without any defect, meaning without leprosy. Then he put it back and it returned to its original color. So he consulted the nobles around him about what he had seen, and they said to him: These are two magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic and do away with your best way, meaning their kingdom that they were in and their livelihood. And they refused to give Moses anything of what he asked for, and they said to him: Gather for them the magicians, for there are many in your land until you overcome their magic with your magic. So he sent to the cities and gathered for him every learned magician. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: What does this magician do? They said: He works with snakes. They said: By God, no one on earth works magic with snakes, ropes and sticks as we do. So what is our reward if we are defeated? He said to them: You are my relatives and my special ones, and I will do for you whatever you like. So they made an appointment on the Day of Adornment and that the people would be gathered at noon. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ibn Abbas told me that the day of adornment was the day on which God gave victory to Moses over Pharaoh and the magicians, which was the day of Ashura. So when they gathered in one place, the people said to one another: Go, let us attend to this matter. Perhaps we will follow the magicians, if they are the ones who are victorious, meaning Moses and Aaron, mocking them. They said, O Moses, either you throw or we will be the ones to throw. He said, Throw. “So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, ‘By the might of Pharaoh, we will surely be the victors.’” Moses saw from their magic what made him fear, so God inspired him to throw down his staff. When he threw it down, it became a huge serpent with its mouth open. The staffs began to entangle themselves with the ropes until they became islands that the serpent entered into until it did not leave a single staff or rope without devouring it. When the magicians realized that, they said, “If this were magic, our magic would not have reached all this, but this is a command from God Almighty. We believe in God and in what Moses brought from God, and we repent to God for what we were doing.” So God broke the back of Pharaoh and his followers in that place, and the truth appeared and what they were doing was nullified. So they were defeated there and returned humiliated. Pharaoh’s wife was prominent and disheveled, calling on God for victory for Moses over Pharaoh and his followers. Whoever from Pharaoh’s family saw her thought that she was only She was humbled to pity Pharaoh and his followers, but her sorrow and concern were for Moses. When Moses remained with Pharaoh’s false promises for a long time, whenever he brought a sign, he promised her that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But when it passed, he broke his promise and said: Can your Lord do anything other than this? So God sent upon his people the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, detailed signs. All of them complained to Moses and asked him to stop them from him and to covenant with him to send the Children of Israel with him. If he stopped them from him, he broke his promise and violated his covenant until God ordered Moses to go out with his people. He went out with them at night. When Pharaoh woke up and saw that they had gone, he sent gatherers to the cities, and he followed him with many great armies. God revealed to the sea, When My servant Moses strikes you with his staff, and it split into twelve divisions until Moses and those with him crossed. Then it converged on those who remained after that from Pharaoh and his followers. Moses forgot to strike the sea with the staff and ended up at the sea, and it had a raging crust, fearing that Moses would strike it with his staff while he was unaware, and he would become disobedient to God. So when the two hosts saw each other and came close together, the companions of Moses said, "We are surely to be overtaken. Do what your Lord has commanded you, for indeed, He has not lied, and you have not lied." He said, My Lord has promised me that when I come to the sea, it will split into twelve divisions so that I may cross it. Then after that he mentioned the staff, so he struck the sea with his staff when the first of Pharaoh's army drew near the last of Moses' army, and the sea split as his Lord had commanded him and as He had promised Moses. When Moses and all his companions had crossed the sea and Pharaoh and his companions had entered, the sea met them as he had been commanded. When Moses had crossed the sea, his companions said, Indeed, we fear that Pharaoh has drowned, and we do not believe in his perishing. So he called upon his Lord, who brought him out for him in his body until they were certain of his perishing. Then after that they passed by a people who were devoted to their idols. "They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. * Indeed, what they are in is ruined.'" You have seen and heard what suffices you. Then he went and Moses settled them in a place and said, "Obey Aaron, for I have made him your successor. I am going to my Lord." And he gave them a respite of thirty days in which he would return to them. So when he came to his Lord and wanted to speak to Him during the thirty days, he had fasted day and night, and he hated to speak to his Lord while the odor of one who is fasting smelled from him. So Moses took some vegetation from the ground and chewed it. Then his Lord said to him when he came to Him, Why have you broken your fast? And He is most knowing of what happened. He said, O Lord, I hated to speak to You except while my mouth smelled good. He said, Did you not know, O Moses, that the odor of one who is fasting is better to Me than the odor of musk? Go back and fast ten days, then come to Me. So Moses, peace be upon him, did what he was ordered to do. When his people saw that he did not return to them within the appointed time, they were upset. Aaron had addressed them and said: You have left Egypt, and Pharaoh’s people have loans and deposits with you, and you have the same with them. I see that you are counting what you have with them, and I do not permit for you a deposit that you have entrusted to you or a loan. We will not return anything of that to them, nor will we keep it for ourselves. So he dug a hole and ordered every people who had any of that, whether it was a commodity or an ornament, to throw it into that hole. Then he lit a fire over it and burned it. He said: It will not be for us or for them. The Samaritan was from a people who worshipped cows, neighbors of the Children of Israel, but he was not from the Children of Israel. So he was carried with Moses and the Children of Israel when they were carried. It was decreed that he saw a trace and took a handful of it. He passed by Aaron, and Aaron, peace be upon him, said to him: O Samaritan, will you not throw away what is in your hand, while he is holding it and no one sees it during that time? He said: This is a handful of the trace of the Messenger who crossed the sea with you, and I will not throw it for anything except that you pray to God when you throw it to make it what I want. So he threw it and Aaron prayed for him, and he said: I want it to be a calf. So everything that was in the pit of goods or ornaments or copper or iron gathered together and it became a hollow calf with no soul in it and it mooed. Ibn Abbas said: No, by God, it never had a voice. Rather, the wind entered its anus and came out of its mouth, and that sound was from that. So the Children of Israel split into groups, and a group said: O Samaritan, what is this and you know best about it? He said: This is your Lord, but Moses has lost his way. A group said: We will not deny this until Moses returns to us. If he is our Lord, we would not have lost him and failed in his cause when we saw him. If he is not our Lord, then we will follow the words of Moses. A group said: This is the work of Satan, and he is not our Lord, and we do not believe in him or believe him. A group imbibed the truth in their hearts with what the Samaritan said about the calf, and they declared their denial of it. Then Aaron said to them: O my people, you are only being tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command. They said: So what is the matter with Moses, that he promised us thirty days and then broke his promise? These forty days have passed. Their fools said: His Lord has made a mistake, so he is seeking him: following him. When God spoke to Moses and told him what He said, He informed him of what his people had encountered after him. So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, and he said to them what you have heard in the Qur’an. He took hold of his brother’s head, dragging him towards him, and threw down the tablets in anger. Then he excused his brother with his excuse and asked forgiveness for him, and went back to the Samaritan. He said to him: What made you do what you did? He said: I took a handful of the Messenger’s trace and understood it, but you were blind to it. “So I cast it aside, and thus my soul enticed me. He said: Then go, for in this life you will have the right to say, ‘No contact,’ and you have an appointment which you will not fail to fulfill. And look to your god, to whom you have been devoted. We will surely burn him and scatter him into the sea as a blast.” Had he been a god, he would not have achieved that from him. The Children of Israel were certain of the trial, and those who had the same opinion of him as Aaron rejoiced, so they said to their group: O Moses, ask your Lord to open for us a door of repentance that we may do, and He will forgive us for what we have done. So Moses chose from his people seventy men who would spare no effort in doing good, the best of the Children of Israel and those who had not associated partners with God in the calf. He set out with them asking for their repentance, and the earth shook under them! The Prophet of God felt ashamed before his people and his delegation when he did to them what he did, so he said: “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done?” Among them were those whom God had seen of the love of the calf and their belief in it that had permeated their hearts, and for that reason the earth shook with them. He said: “And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses - those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written down in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel.” So he said: “O Lord, I asked You for repentance for my people, and You said that My mercy was written for a people other than my people. Why did You not delay me until You bring me out into the nation of that man who has been shown mercy?” He said to him: Their repentance is that each man among them kills whoever he meets of father and son, killing him with the sword and not caring who he kills in that place. Those who were hidden from Moses and Aaron repented, and God saw their sins, so they confessed to them and did what they were commanded, and God forgave the killer and the one killed. Then Moses, peace be upon him, walked with them towards the Holy Land, and took the tablets after his anger subsided, and ordered them to do what he ordered them to do of the duties, but that was heavy on them and they refused to acknowledge it, so God made the mountain appear to them as if it were a canopy and approached them until they feared it would fall on them, so they took the book in their right hands while they were listening, looking at the mountain and the book in their hands while they were behind the mountain for fear that it would fall on them, then they went until they came to the Holy Land and found a city in which there were tyrannical people, their creation was strange, and they mentioned from their fruits something amazing about its size, so they said: O Moses, there are tyrannical people in it that we cannot bear, and we will not enter it as long as they are in it, but if they leave it, then we will enter. Two men from those who feared said: It was said to Yazid: Did he read it like this? He said: Yes, from the tyrants we believed in Moses and they went out to him and said: We know our people best. If you only fear what you have seen of their bodies and their numbers, then they have no hearts and no strength, so enter upon them through the gate, and when you enter it, you will be victorious. And some people say: They are from the people of Moses. So those who feared from the Children of Israel said: They said: O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here. So they angered Moses, so he invoked against them and called them wicked, and he had not invoked against them before that when he saw their disobedience and their wrongdoing until that day, so God answered him and called them as Moses had called them wicked, and forbade them from it for forty years, wandering in the land, waking up every day and walking, with no resting place. And He shaded them with clouds in the wilderness, and sent down upon them manna and quails, and made for them clothes that would not wear out or get dirty, and He placed a square stone among them, and commanded Moses to strike it. With his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from it, three springs in each direction, and he informed each tribe of the spring from which they would drink, and they would not move from one place except that they would find that stone among them in the place where it had been the day before. Ibn Abbas traced this hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I believe that Muawiyah heard Ibn Abbas narrating this hadith and he denied that the Pharaoh was the one who disclosed to Moses the matter of the one killed. He said: How could he disclose it to him when he had no knowledge of it and no one was present at it except the Israelite who was present? Ibn Abbas became angry and took Muawiyah by the hand and went with him to Sa`d ibn Malik al-Zuhri and said to him: O Abu Ishaq, do you remember the day when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us about the one killed by Moses from the family of Pharaoh? Was it the Israelite who disclosed it or the Pharaoh? He said: The Pharaoh only revealed to him what he heard from the Israelite who witnessed and was present at that. This is how al-Nasa’i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim included it in their interpretations, all of them from the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun with it, and it is attributed to Ibn Abbas, and there is nothing in it that is attributed to the Prophet except a little of it, and it seems that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, received it from what was permitted to be transmitted from the Israelite narrations from Ka’b al-Ahbar, or someone else, and God knows best. I heard our Sheikh, the preserver Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, say that as well. And the Almighty said:
20:38: This is an answer from God to His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, regarding what he asked of his Lord, the Almighty, and a reminder to him of His previous blessings upon him regarding what happened with his mother when she was breastfeeding him and warning him against Pharaoh and his people killing him, because he was born in the year in which they kill boys, so she made a coffin for him, and she was breastfeeding him and then putting him in it and sending him into the sea, which is the Nile, and holding him to her home with a rope, so she went once to tie the rope and it slipped from her and the sea took him, so she experienced the grief and worry that God mentioned about her in His saying: “And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty. She would have almost disclosed him had We not strengthened her heart.” So the sea took him to Pharaoh’s house. Then Pharaoh’s family picked him up to become for them an enemy and a grief, meaning a decree decreed by God, as they were killing the boys of the Children of Israel out of fear of Moses’ presence, so God decreed, and He has the great authority and complete power, that he would not be raised except on Pharaoh’s bed, and would be fed. With his food and drink, along with his wife’s love for him, and for this reason the Almighty said: An enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him, and I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning upon your enemy I made him love you. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: And I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning: I made you beloved to My servants. And that you may be brought up before My eyes, Abu Imran al-Jawni said: He was raised in the eye of God. Qatada said: He was fed before My eyes. Muammar ibn al-Muthanna said: And that you may be brought up before My eyes, so that I may see. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Meaning: I will make him live in the king’s house, enjoying himself and being pampered, and his food with them is the food of the king, so that is the craft. And His saying: “And when your sister walked and said: ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?’ So We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted.” That is because when he settled with the people of Pharaoh, they offered him wet nurses, but he refused. God Almighty said: And We had forbidden him wet nurses before. So his sister came and said: Shall I direct you to a family who will take care of him for you and be sincere to him? Meaning: Shall I direct you to someone who will breastfeed him for you for a fee? So she went with him and they were with her to his mother, and she offered him her breast, and he accepted it. They were very happy with that, and they hired her to breastfeed him, so she attained happiness, elevation, and comfort because of him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will be richer and more abundant. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith: The example of the craftsman who expects good in his craft is like the example of the mother of Moses who breastfeeds her son and takes her wages. And God Almighty said here: And We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted and she not grieve, meaning for you. And you killed a soul, meaning the Copt. And We saved you from distress, which is what happened to him because of his determination. Pharaoh's family wanted to kill him, so he fled from them until he reached the water of Madyan. That righteous man said to him: Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. And his saying: And We have tried you with trials. Imam Abu Abdul Rahman Ahmad bin Shuaib Al-Nasa’i, may God have mercy on him, said in the book of interpretation from his Sunan: His saying And We have tried you with trials Hadith of the trials: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Asbagh bin Zaid told us, Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me: I asked Abdullah bin Abbas about the saying of God Almighty to Moses, peace be upon him: And We have tried you with trials. So I asked him about the trials, what are they? He said: Start the day again, O Ibn Jubair, for they have a long story. So when morning came, I went to Ibn Abbas to complete what he promised me about the hadith of the trials. He said: Pharaoh and his companions were discussing what God had promised Abraham, peace be upon him, that He would make prophets and kings among his descendants. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are waiting for that and they have no doubt about it, and they thought that he was Joseph, son of Jacob. So when he died, they said: This is not how Abraham was promised, peace be upon him. So Pharaoh said: What do you think? So they plotted and agreed that he would send men with knives to go around among the Children of Israel and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. So they did that. When they saw that the adults of the Children of Israel were dying at their appointed times and the young were being slaughtered, they said: You are about to annihilate the Children of Israel and you will be at the point where you will be able to do the work and service that they used to do for you. So kill every male child one year and leave their daughters alone, and leave one year and do not kill any of them, so that the young will grow up in place of those who die from the adults. They will not increase in number because of those whom you are ashamed of, so that you will fear their increasing number with you, and they will not be destroyed because of those whom you kill and need. So they agreed on that. So Moses’ mother became pregnant with Aaron in the year in which boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. Then the following year, she became pregnant with Moses, peace be upon him, and worry and sadness fell into her heart. That is from the trials - O Ibn Jubayr - that which came upon him while he was in his mother’s womb, which is intended. Then God revealed to her, "Do not fear and do not grieve. We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers." So He commanded her, when she gave birth, to put him in a coffin and then throw him into the sea. So when she gave birth, she did that. Then, when her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her and she said to herself, What have you done with my son? If he were slaughtered here and I buried him and shrouded him, that would be more beloved to me than to throw him to the beasts and whales of the sea. The water reached him until it reached the watering place of the maids of Pharaoh's wife. When they saw him, they seized him and wanted to open the chest. Some of them said: There is money in this, and if we open it, the king's wife will not believe us with what we found in it. So they carried it as it was and did not take anything out of it until they gave it to her. When she opened it, she saw a boy in it, and God bestowed upon him a love from her that He had never bestowed upon anyone before. The heart of Moses' mother became empty of remembering everything except the mention of Moses. When the slaughterers heard of his command, they came with their knives to Pharaoh's wife to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. She said to them: Leave him alone, for this one will not increase the number of the Children of Israel until I go to Pharaoh and ask him for his gift. If he gives him to me, you will have done well and acted well, but if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you. So she went to Pharaoh and said: A delight to me and you. Pharaoh said: He will be for you, but as for me, I have no need of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And by Him he swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be the comfort of his eye as his wife had acknowledged, God would have guided him as he had guided her, but He deprived him of that. So she sent to those around her, to every woman who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him. But whenever one of them took him to breastfeed him, he would not accept her breast until Pharaoh’s wife feared that he would refuse milk and die. That saddened her, so she ordered him to be taken out to the market and the assembly of people, hoping that she would find a wet nurse for him to take from her, but he did not accept. Moses' mother became obsessed and said to his sister: "Follow him and look for him. Do you hear him say, 'Is my son alive or has the beasts eaten him?'" She forgot what God had promised her. His sister saw him from afar, and they were unaware. Afar is when a person's eyes look at something far away, but it is beside him, and he is unaware of it. So she said out of joy when the wet nurses were exhausted: I will show you a household that will take care of him for you and will be sincere to him. So they took her and said, How do you know that they were sincere to him? Do they know him? Until they doubted that, and that is from the temptations, O Ibn Jubayr. So she said: Their advice to him and their compassion for him, their desire for the king’s wet nurse and the hope of the king’s benefit, so they left her. So she went to her mother and told her the report. So his mother came and when she placed him in her lap, he climbed onto her breast and sucked it until his sides were filled with moisture. And the good report went to Pharaoh’s wife to give her the good report that we have found a wet nurse for your son. So she sent to her and brought her and him. When she saw what was being done to her, she said: Stay and nurse this son of mine, for I have never loved anything as much as he has loved. Moses' mother said: I cannot leave my house and my son to be lost. If you are willing to give him to me, I will take him to my house and he will be with me. I will spare no good for him, for I will not leave my house and my son. Moses' mother remembered what God had promised her, and she felt sorry for Pharaoh's wife and was certain that God would fulfill His promise. She returned with him to her house that day, and God made him grow well and preserved him for what He had decreed for him. The children of Israel, who were in the outskirts of the village, remained free from the oppression and injustice that was among them. When he grew up, Pharaoh’s wife said to Moses’ mother: Will you show me my son? So she called her for a day in which she could show him to her. Pharaoh’s wife said to her keepers, wet nurses, and maidservants: “Let not one of you remain without receiving my son today with a gift and honor so that I may see that. I am sending a trustee to record what each one of you does.” So gifts, honor, and gifts continued to greet him from the time he left his mother’s house until he entered upon Pharaoh’s wife. When he entered upon her, she honored him and was pleased with him, and his mother bestowed gifts because of her good influence on him. Then she said: Let us bring him to Pharaoh so that he may bestow gifts upon him and honor him. So when she entered upon him, he placed him in his lap. Moses took Pharaoh’s beard and stretched it to the ground. Then the seducers from among the enemies of God said to Pharaoh: “Do you not see what God promised His prophet Abraham? He claimed that he would inherit you, rise above you, and defeat you. So he sent for the slaughterers to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr after every calamity he was afflicted with. And he wanted to cause trials, so Pharaoh's wife came and said: What do you want with this boy whom you gave me? He said: Do you not see that he claims that he can wrestle with me and be superior to me? She said: Make a matter between me and you by which the truth will be known. Bring two live coals and two pearls and present them to him. If he grabs the two pearls and avoids the live coals, you will know that he is sane. But if he takes the live coals and does not want the pearls, you will know that no one would prefer the live coals to the pearls while he is sane. So the live coals and the pearls were brought to him, and he took the live coals and snatched them away from him for fear that they would burn his hand. The woman said: Do you not see? Then God turned him away from him after he had intended to do it, and God accomplished His command with him, and when he reached his full maturity and was a man, no one from the family of Pharaoh would get to any of the Children of Israel with him by oppression or force, until they refused completely. While Moses, peace be upon him, was walking in the direction of the city, he saw two men fighting, one of them a Pharaoh and the other an Israelite. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, and Moses became very angry, because he attacked him while he knew his status among the Children of Israel and his protection of them, and no one knew except that it was from breastfeeding except Moses’ mother, unless God informed Moses of that which no one else knew. So Moses struck the Pharaoh and killed him, and no one saw them except God, the Almighty, and the Israelite. Moses said when he killed the man: This is from the work of Satan, he is a clear, misleading enemy. Then he said: “My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me.” So He forgave him, for He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. So he stayed in the city, afraid, waiting for report. Then he came to Pharaoh and it was said to him: The Children of Israel killed a man from the family of Pharaoh, so take our right for us and do not give them concessions. He said: Find me his killer and someone who can testify against him, for the king, even if he is on good terms with his people, cannot be bound without evidence or proof. So seek knowledge of that for me and I will take your right for you. While they were wandering around and finding no proof, Moses saw the next day that Israelite fighting a man from the family of another Pharaoh. The Israelite called for help from him against the Pharaoh, but he came across Moses and regretted what he had done and hated what he had seen. The Israelite became angry and wanted to strike the Pharaoh. So he said to the Israelite for what he had done yesterday and today: You are clearly a liar. The Israelite looked at Moses after he had said what he had said to him, and he was as angry as he had been the day before when he had killed the Pharaoh. He feared that after he had said to him that you are a clear liar, he had meant him and had not meant him, but rather he meant the Pharaoh. The Israelite became afraid and said: O Moses, do you want to He said this out of fear that Moses wanted to kill him. So they parted ways and the Pharaoh went and told them what he had heard from the Israelite when he said: O Moses, do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? So Fu’un sent the slaughterers to kill Moses. So the messengers of Pharaoh took the main road, walking at their own pace, seeking Moses, not fearing that they would miss him. Then a man from Moses’ party came from the farthest part of the city, and he took a shortcut until he reached Moses before them and told him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. Moses set out towards Madyan, and he had not encountered any calamity before that, and he had no knowledge of the road except his good opinion of his Lord, the Almighty, for he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way. And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their flocks, and he found besides them two women holding back their sheep. So he said to them: What is the matter with you, that you are isolated and not watering your flocks with the people? They said: We do not have the strength to compete with the people, but we drink from the excess of their watering place. So he watered for them and began to scoop up a lot of water in the bucket until he was the first of the shepherds. Then they returned with their sheep to their father, and Moses, peace be upon him, returned and took shelter under a tree and said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need. Their father was surprised at their quick return with their sheep, full and content, so he said: You have a matter today. So they told him what Moses had done. So he ordered one of them to call him, so she went to Moses and called him. When he spoke to him, he said: “Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom.” One of them said: “O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.” So jealousy made him say to her: How do you know what his strength is or how trustworthy he is? She said: As for his strength, I did not see him in the bucket when he watered for us. I have never seen a man stronger in that watering than him. As for his trustworthiness, he looked at me when I came to him and looked at him, and when he knew that I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it until I delivered your message to him. Then he said to me: Walk behind me and describe the way to me. He did this only because he is trustworthy. So her father was pleased and believed her and thought of him what she said. So he said to him: Would you like me to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you hire me for eight years. If you complete ten, it will be from you. I do not want to make it difficult for you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous? So he did so. Eight years were obligatory for the Prophet of God, Moses, and two years were his waiting period. So God fulfilled his waiting period and he completed it to ten. Saeed, who is Ibn Jubayr, said: A Christian scholar met me and said: Do you know which of the two terms Moses fulfilled? I said: No, and I did not know at that time. So I met Ibn Abbas and mentioned that to him, and he said: Did you not know that eight were obligatory upon the Prophet of God, and the Prophet of God would not decrease anything from them, and he knows that God was fulfilling the promise that He had made for Moses, for he fulfilled ten years. So I met the Christian and told him that, and he said: The one whom you asked and he informed you knows more about that than you. I said: Yes, and more appropriate. So when Moses set out with his family, there was something about the fire, the staff, and his hand that God has told you about in the Qur’an. So he complained to God Almighty about what he feared from the family of Pharaoh regarding the one killed and the knot of his tongue, for there was a knot in his tongue that prevented him from speaking much, and he asked his Lord to help him with his brother Aaron to be a support for him and to speak on his behalf much of what his tongue could not express. So God granted him his request and loosened the knot from his tongue, and God inspired Aaron and commanded him to meet him, so Moses rushed with his staff until he met Aaron, peace be upon them, and they both went to Pharaoh, and they stayed on His door was closed for a while, but they were not given permission. Then he gave them permission after a severe veil. They said: We are messengers of your Lord. He said: Who is your Lord? So tell him what God has told you in the Qur’an. He said: What do you want? The dead man mentioned to him and apologized for what he had heard. He said: I want you to believe in God and send the Children of Israel with us. But he refused and said: Bring a sign if you are of the truthful. So he threw down his staff and behold, it was a great, darting serpent, opening its mouth, rushing toward Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw it heading toward him, he was afraid of it and rushed from his bed and called upon Moses to stop it from him, and he did so. Then he took his hand out of his pocket and saw it white without any defect, meaning without leprosy. Then he put it back and it returned to its original color. So he consulted the nobles around him about what he had seen, and they said to him: These are two magicians who want to expel you from your land with their magic and do away with your best way, meaning their kingdom that they were in and their livelihood. And they refused to give Moses anything of what he asked for, and they said to him: Gather for them the magicians, for there are many in your land until you overcome their magic with your magic. So he sent to the cities and gathered for him every learned magician. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: What does this magician do? They said: He works with snakes. They said: By God, no one on earth works magic with snakes, ropes and sticks as we do. So what is our reward if we are defeated? He said to them: You are my relatives and my special ones, and I will do for you whatever you like. So they made an appointment on the Day of Adornment and that the people would be gathered at noon. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ibn Abbas told me that the day of adornment was the day on which God gave victory to Moses over Pharaoh and the magicians, which was the day of Ashura. So when they gathered in one place, the people said to one another: Go, let us attend to this matter. Perhaps we will follow the magicians, if they are the ones who are victorious, meaning Moses and Aaron, mocking them. They said, O Moses, either you throw or we will be the ones to throw. He said, Throw. “So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, ‘By the might of Pharaoh, we will surely be the victors.’” Moses saw from their magic what made him fear, so God inspired him to throw down his staff. When he threw it down, it became a huge serpent with its mouth open. The staffs began to entangle themselves with the ropes until they became islands that the serpent entered into until it did not leave a single staff or rope without devouring it. When the magicians realized that, they said, “If this were magic, our magic would not have reached all this, but this is a command from God Almighty. We believe in God and in what Moses brought from God, and we repent to God for what we were doing.” So God broke the back of Pharaoh and his followers in that place, and the truth appeared and what they were doing was nullified. So they were defeated there and returned humiliated. Pharaoh’s wife was prominent and disheveled, calling on God for victory for Moses over Pharaoh and his followers. Whoever from Pharaoh’s family saw her thought that she was only She was humbled to pity Pharaoh and his followers, but her sorrow and concern were for Moses. When Moses remained with Pharaoh’s false promises for a long time, whenever he brought a sign, he promised her that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But when it passed, he broke his promise and said: Can your Lord do anything other than this? So God sent upon his people the flood, locusts, lice, frogs and blood, detailed signs. All of them complained to Moses and asked him to stop them from him and to covenant with him to send the Children of Israel with him. If he stopped them from him, he broke his promise and violated his covenant until God ordered Moses to go out with his people. He went out with them at night. When Pharaoh woke up and saw that they had gone, he sent gatherers to the cities, and he followed him with many great armies. God revealed to the sea, When My servant Moses strikes you with his staff, and it split into twelve divisions until Moses and those with him crossed. Then it converged on those who remained after that from Pharaoh and his followers. Moses forgot to strike the sea with the staff and ended up at the sea, and it had a raging crust, fearing that Moses would strike it with his staff while he was unaware, and he would become disobedient to God. So when the two hosts saw each other and came close together, the companions of Moses said, "We are surely to be overtaken. Do what your Lord has commanded you, for indeed, He has not lied, and you have not lied." He said, My Lord has promised me that when I come to the sea, it will split into twelve divisions so that I may cross it. Then after that he mentioned the staff, so he struck the sea with his staff when the first of Pharaoh's army drew near the last of Moses' army, and the sea split as his Lord had commanded him and as He had promised Moses. When Moses and all his companions had crossed the sea and Pharaoh and his companions had entered, the sea met them as he had been commanded. When Moses had crossed the sea, his companions said, Indeed, we fear that Pharaoh has drowned, and we do not believe in his perishing. So he called upon his Lord, who brought him out for him in his body until they were certain of his perishing. Then after that they passed by a people who were devoted to their idols. "They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. * Indeed, what they are in is ruined.'" You have seen and heard what suffices you. Then he went and Moses settled them in a place and said, "Obey Aaron, for I have made him your successor. I am going to my Lord." And he gave them a respite of thirty days in which he would return to them. So when he came to his Lord and wanted to speak to Him during the thirty days, he had fasted day and night, and he hated to speak to his Lord while the odor of one who is fasting smelled from him. So Moses took some vegetation from the ground and chewed it. Then his Lord said to him when he came to Him, Why have you broken your fast? And He is most knowing of what happened. He said, O Lord, I hated to speak to You except while my mouth smelled good. He said, Did you not know, O Moses, that the odor of one who is fasting is better to Me than the odor of musk? Go back and fast ten days, then come to Me. So Moses, peace be upon him, did what he was ordered to do. When his people saw that he did not return to them within the appointed time, they were upset. Aaron had addressed them and said: You have left Egypt, and Pharaoh’s people have loans and deposits with you, and you have the same with them. I see that you are counting what you have with them, and I do not permit for you a deposit that you have entrusted to you or a loan. We will not return anything of that to them, nor will we keep it for ourselves. So he dug a hole and ordered every people who had any of that, whether it was a commodity or an ornament, to throw it into that hole. Then he lit a fire over it and burned it. He said: It will not be for us or for them. The Samaritan was from a people who worshipped cows, neighbors of the Children of Israel, but he was not from the Children of Israel. So he was carried with Moses and the Children of Israel when they were carried. It was decreed that he saw a trace and took a handful of it. He passed by Aaron, and Aaron, peace be upon him, said to him: O Samaritan, will you not throw away what is in your hand, while he is holding it and no one sees it during that time? He said: This is a handful of the trace of the Messenger who crossed the sea with you, and I will not throw it for anything except that you pray to God when you throw it to make it what I want. So he threw it and Aaron prayed for him, and he said: I want it to be a calf. So everything that was in the pit of goods or ornaments or copper or iron gathered together and it became a hollow calf with no soul in it and it mooed. Ibn Abbas said: No, by God, it never had a voice. Rather, the wind entered its anus and came out of its mouth, and that sound was from that. So the Children of Israel split into groups, and a group said: O Samaritan, what is this and you know best about it? He said: This is your Lord, but Moses has lost his way. A group said: We will not deny this until Moses returns to us. If he is our Lord, we would not have lost him and failed in his cause when we saw him. If he is not our Lord, then we will follow the words of Moses. A group said: This is the work of Satan, and he is not our Lord, and we do not believe in him or believe him. A group imbibed the truth in their hearts with what the Samaritan said about the calf, and they declared their denial of it. Then Aaron said to them: O my people, you are only being tested by it, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command. They said: So what is the matter with Moses, that he promised us thirty days and then broke his promise? These forty days have passed. Their fools said: His Lord has made a mistake, so he is seeking him: following him. When God spoke to Moses and told him what He said, He informed him of what his people had encountered after him. So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, and he said to them what you have heard in the Qur’an. He took hold of his brother’s head, dragging him towards him, and threw down the tablets in anger. Then he excused his brother with his excuse and asked forgiveness for him, and went back to the Samaritan. He said to him: What made you do what you did? He said: I took a handful of the Messenger’s trace and understood it, but you were blind to it. “So I cast it aside, and thus my soul enticed me. He said: Then go, for in this life you will have the right to say, ‘No contact,’ and you have an appointment which you will not fail to fulfill. And look to your god, to whom you have been devoted. We will surely burn him and scatter him into the sea as a blast.” Had he been a god, he would not have achieved that from him. The Children of Israel were certain of the trial, and those who had the same opinion of him as Aaron rejoiced, so they said to their group: O Moses, ask your Lord to open for us a door of repentance that we may do, and He will forgive us for what we have done. So Moses chose from his people seventy men who would spare no effort in doing good, the best of the Children of Israel and those who had not associated partners with God in the calf. He set out with them asking for their repentance, and the earth shook under them! The Prophet of God felt ashamed before his people and his delegation when he did to them what he did, so he said: “My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done?” Among them were those whom God had seen of the love of the calf and their belief in it that had permeated their hearts, and for that reason the earth shook with them. He said: “And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our verses - those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written down in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel.” So he said: “O Lord, I asked You for repentance for my people, and You said that My mercy was written for a people other than my people. Why did You not delay me until You bring me out into the nation of that man who has been shown mercy?” He said to him: Their repentance is that each man among them kills whoever he meets of father and son, killing him with the sword and not caring who he kills in that place. Those who were hidden from Moses and Aaron repented, and God saw their sins, so they confessed to them and did what they were commanded, and God forgave the killer and the one killed. Then Moses, peace be upon him, walked with them towards the Holy Land, and took the tablets after his anger subsided, and ordered them to do what he ordered them to do of the duties, but that was heavy on them and they refused to acknowledge it, so God made the mountain appear to them as if it were a canopy and approached them until they feared it would fall on them, so they took the book in their right hands while they were listening, looking at the mountain and the book in their hands while they were behind the mountain for fear that it would fall on them, then they went until they came to the Holy Land and found a city in which there were tyrannical people, their creation was strange, and they mentioned from their fruits something amazing about its size, so they said: O Moses, there are tyrannical people in it that we cannot bear, and we will not enter it as long as they are in it, but if they leave it, then we will enter. Two men from those who feared said: It was said to Yazid: Did he read it like this? He said: Yes, from the tyrants we believed in Moses and they went out to him and said: We know our people best. If you only fear what you have seen of their bodies and their numbers, then they have no hearts and no strength, so enter upon them through the gate, and when you enter it, you will be victorious. And some people say: They are from the people of Moses. So those who feared from the Children of Israel said: They said: O Moses, we will never enter it as long as they are in it, so go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are sitting right here. So they angered Moses, so he invoked against them and called them wicked, and he had not invoked against them before that when he saw their disobedience and their wrongdoing until that day, so God answered him and called them as Moses had called them wicked, and forbade them from it for forty years, wandering in the land, waking up every day and walking, with no resting place. And He shaded them with clouds in the wilderness, and sent down upon them manna and quails, and made for them clothes that would not wear out or get dirty, and He placed a square stone among them, and commanded Moses to strike it. With his staff, twelve springs gushed forth from it, three springs in each direction, and he informed each tribe of the spring from which they would drink, and they would not move from one place except that they would find that stone among them in the place where it had been the day before. Ibn Abbas traced this hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I believe that Muawiyah heard Ibn Abbas narrating this hadith and he denied that the Pharaoh was the one who disclosed to Moses the matter of the one killed. He said: How could he disclose it to him when he had no knowledge of it and no one was present at it except the Israelite who was present? Ibn Abbas became angry and took Muawiyah by the hand and went with him to Sa`d ibn Malik al-Zuhri and said to him: O Abu Ishaq, do you remember the day when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us about the one killed by Moses from the family of Pharaoh? Was it the Israelite who disclosed it or the Pharaoh? He said: The Pharaoh only revealed to him what he heard from the Israelite who witnessed and was present at that. This is how al-Nasa’i narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim included it in their interpretations, all of them from the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun with it, and it is attributed to Ibn Abbas, and there is nothing in it that is attributed to the Prophet except a little of it, and it seems that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, received it from what was permitted to be transmitted from the Israelite narrations from Ka’b al-Ahbar, or someone else, and God knows best. I heard our Sheikh, the preserver Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, say that as well. And the Almighty said:
20:39: This is an answer from God to His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him, regarding what he asked of his Lord, the Almighty, and a reminder to him of His previous blessings upon him regarding what happened with his mother when she was breastfeeding him and warning him against Pharaoh and his people killing him, because he was born in the year in which they kill boys, so she made a coffin for him, and she was breastfeeding him and then putting him in it and sending him into the sea, which is the Nile, and holding him to her home with a rope, so she went once to tie the rope and it slipped from her and the sea took him, so she experienced the grief and worry that God mentioned about her in His saying: “And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty. She would have almost disclosed him had We not strengthened her heart.” So the sea took him to Pharaoh’s house. Then Pharaoh’s family picked him up to become for them an enemy and a grief, meaning a decree decreed by God, as they were killing the boys of the Children of Israel out of fear of Moses’ presence, so God decreed, and He has the great authority and complete power, that he would not be raised except on Pharaoh’s bed, and would be fed. With his food and drink, along with his wife’s love for him, and for this reason the Almighty said: An enemy of Mine and an enemy of his will take him, and I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning upon your enemy I made him love you. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: And I bestowed upon you love from Me, meaning: I made you beloved to My servants. And that you may be brought up before My eyes, Abu Imran al-Jawni said: He was raised in the eye of God. Qatada said: He was fed before My eyes. Muammar ibn al-Muthanna said: And that you may be brought up before My eyes, so that I may see. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Meaning: I will make him live in the king’s house, enjoying himself and being pampered, and his food with them is the food of the king, so that is the craft. And His saying: “And when your sister walked and said: ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?’ So We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted.” That is because when he settled with the people of Pharaoh, they offered him wet nurses, but he refused. God Almighty said: And We had forbidden him wet nurses before. So his sister came and said: Shall I direct you to a family who will take care of him for you and be sincere to him? Meaning: Shall I direct you to someone who will breastfeed him for you for a fee? So she went with him and they were with her to his mother, and she offered him her breast, and he accepted it. They were very happy with that, and they hired her to breastfeed him, so she attained happiness, elevation, and comfort because of him in this world, and in the Hereafter he will be richer and more abundant. For this reason, it was stated in the hadith: The example of the craftsman who expects good in his craft is like the example of the mother of Moses who breastfeeds her son and takes her wages. And God Almighty said here: And We returned you to your mother that her eye may be comforted and she not grieve, meaning for you. And you killed a soul, meaning the Copt. And We saved you from distress, which is what happened to him because of his determination. Pharaoh's family wanted to kill him, so he fled from them until he reached the water of Madyan. That righteous man said to him: Do not fear, you have escaped from the unjust people. And his saying: And We have tried you with trials. Imam Abu Abdul Rahman Ahmad bin Shuaib Al-Nasa’i, may God have mercy on him, said in the book of interpretation from his Sunan: His saying And We have tried you with trials Hadith of the trials: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Asbagh bin Zaid told us, Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayoub told us, Saeed bin Jubair told me: I asked Abdullah bin Abbas about the saying of God Almighty to Moses, peace be upon him: And We have tried you with trials. So I asked him about the trials, what are they? He said: Start the day again, O Ibn Jubair, for they have a long story. So when morning came, I went to Ibn Abbas to complete what he promised me about the hadith of the trials. He said: Pharaoh and his companions were discussing what God had promised Abraham, peace be upon him, that He would make prophets and kings among his descendants. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are waiting for that and they have no doubt about it, and they thought that he was Joseph, son of Jacob. So when he died, they said: This is not how Abraham was promised, peace be upon him. So Pharaoh said: What do you think? So they plotted and agreed that he would send men with knives to go around among the Children of Israel and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. So they did that. When they saw that the adults of the Children of Israel were dying at their appointed times and the young were being slaughtered, they said: You are about to annihilate the Children of Israel and you will be at the point where you will be able to do the work and service that they used to do for you. So kill every male child one year and leave their daughters alone, and leave one year and do not kill any of them, so that the young will grow up in place of those who die from the adults. They will not increase in number because of those whom you are ashamed of, so that you will fear their increasing number with you, and they will not be destroyed because of those whom you kill and need. So they agreed on that. So Moses’ mother became pregnant with Aaron in the year in which boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. Then the following year, she became pregnant with Moses, peace be upon him, and worry and sadness fell into her heart. That is from the trials - O Ibn Jubayr - that which came upon him while he was in his mother’s womb, which is intended. Then God revealed to her, "Do not fear and do not grieve. We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers." So He commanded her, when she gave birth, to put him in a coffin and then throw him into the sea. So when she gave birth, she did that. Then, when her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her and she said to herself, What have you done with my son? If he were slaughtered here and I buried him and shrouded him, that would be more beloved to me than to throw him to the beasts and whales of the sea. The water reached him until it reached the watering place of the maids of Pharaoh's wife. When they saw him, they seized him and wanted to open the chest. Some of them said: There is money in this, and if we open it, the king's wife will not believe us with what we found in it. So they carried it as it was and did not take anything out of it until they gave it to her. When she opened it, she saw a boy in it, and God bestowed upon him a love from her that He had never bestowed upon anyone before. The heart of Moses' mother became empty of remembering everything except the mention of Moses. When the slaughterers heard of his command, they came with their knives to Pharaoh's wife to slaughter him. That is one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr. She said to them: Leave him alone, for this one will not increase the number of the Children of Israel until I go to Pharaoh and ask him for his gift. If he gives him to me, you will have done well and acted well, but if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you. So she went to Pharaoh and said: A delight to me and you. Pharaoh said: He will be for you, but as for me, I have no need of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And by Him he swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be the comfort of his eye as his wife had acknowledged, God would have guided him as he had guided her, but He deprived him of that. So she sent to those around her, to every woman who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him. But whenever one of them took him to breastfeed him, he would not accept her breast until Pharaoh’s wife feared that he would refuse milk and die. That saddened her, so she ordered him to be taken out to the market and the assembly of people, hoping that she would find a wet nurse for him to take from her, but he did not accept. Moses' mother became obsessed and said to his sister: "Follow him and look for him. Do you hear him say, 'Is my son alive or has the beasts eaten him?'" She forgot what God had promised her.
