20:53: From the completion of Moses' speech in what he described his Lord, the Almighty, when Pharaoh asked him about it, he said: "Who gave to each thing its form and then guided it." Then he interrupted the speech between that, then he said: "Who made the earth a cradle for you." And in the reading of some of them, it is a cradle, meaning a place where you settle, stand and sleep on, and travel on its back. "And made paths for you therein." That is, He made paths for you to walk in its paths, as God Almighty said: "And We made therein paths, so that they may be guided. And sent down water from the sky, and We produced thereby pairs of diverse plants." That is, of the types of plants, from crops and fruits, and from sour, sweet, bitter, and all other types. "Eat and pasture your livestock." That is, something for your food and fruit, and something for your livestock for their sustenance, green and dry. "Indeed in that are signs." That is, indications, arguments, and proofs. "For those of understanding." That is, for those of sound, upright minds, on There is no god but God and no lord but Him. From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time. That is, from the earth is your beginning, for your father Adam was created from dust from the surface of the earth, and into it We will return you, that is, to it you will go when you die and decay, and from it We will extract you another time. On the Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you remained only a little. This verse is like the saying of God the Almighty: He said, ‘Therein you will live, and therein you will die, and from it you will be extracted.’ In the hadith in the Sunan, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, attended a funeral, and when the dead person was buried, he took a handful of dirt and threw it into the grave and said: From it We created you, then he took another and said: And into it We will return you, then another, and he said: And from it We will extract you another time. And His statement: And We showed him all Our signs, but he denied and refused. This means that Pharaoh was confronted with the arguments, signs, and evidence, and he witnessed and saw that, but he denied them and refused them out of disbelief, stubbornness, and transgression, as God Almighty said: And they denied them, although their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance.

20:57: God Almighty says, informing about Pharaoh, that he said to Moses when he showed him the greatest sign, which was throwing his staff and it became a great serpent, and he pulled his hand from under his wing and it came out white without any harm, so he said: This is magic that you have brought to bewitch us and to take control of the people so that they will follow you, and to multiply us by them, and this will not happen with you, for we have magic like your magic, so do not be deceived by what you are doing, so make an appointment between us and you meaning a day when we and you will meet, so we will oppose what you have brought with what we have of magic in a specific place and a specific time, then Moses said to them your appointment is on the day of adornment which is the day of their festival and their Newroz and their devotion from their work and their gathering together, so that the people may witness the power of God to do what He wills and the miracles of the prophets and the invalidity of the opposition of magic to the extraordinary customs of the prophets, and for this reason He said: and that the people will be gathered meaning all of them at noon meaning at noon of the day, so that it will be more apparent and clear and more evident, and this is how it is The Prophets' affair is all clear and evident, with no concealment or promotion. That is why He did not say at night, but during the day, in the forenoon. Ibn Abbas said: The day of adornment was the day of Ashura. As-Suddi, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd said: It was their festival day. Saeed bin Jubair said: It was their market day, and there is no contradiction. I said: And on the same day God destroyed Pharaoh and his soldiers, as is proven in Sahih. Wahb bin Munabbih said: Pharaoh said: O Moses, set a time limit between us and you that we may consider. Moses said: I was not commanded to do this, rather I was commanded to fight you. If you do not come out, I will come to you. So God revealed to Moses: Set a time limit between you and him, and tell him to set it himself. Pharaoh said: Set it to forty days, so he did. Mujahid and Qatadah said: A place that is even and fair. As-Suddi said: Just. Abd al-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam said: A place that is even and level between the people and what is in it, so that there is no direction or anything that disappears from some of it, level when seen.

20:60: God Almighty says, informing about Pharaoh, that when he and Moses, peace be upon him, had an appointment at a specific time and place, he took over, that is, he began to gather the magicians from the cities of his kingdom, everyone who was attributed to magic at that time, and magic was very common among them, as God Almighty said: And Pharaoh said, ‘Bring me every learned magician.’ Then he came. That is, the people gathered for a specific day, which was the day of adornment, and Pharaoh sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the leaders of his state lined up for him, and the subjects stood to the right and left, and Moses, peace be upon him, came leaning on his staff with his brother Aaron, and the magicians stood in rows before Pharaoh, and he urged them and urged them and encouraged them to do their work well on that day, and they hoped for him while he promised them and hoped for them, saying, Will there be a reward for us if we are the victors? He said, “Yes, and then you will be among those brought near. “Moses said to them, ‘Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God,’” that is, do not imagine to people through your actions that you have created things that have no reality and that they are created, but they are not created, for you will have lied about God, He will destroy you with a punishment, that is, He will destroy you with a punishment that will have no end, “And he who invents has failed. So they disputed their affair among themselves.” It was said that its meaning was that they quarrelled among themselves, so someone said, This is not the speech of a magician, rather this is the speech of a magician. A prophet, and someone says he is a magician, and something else has been said, and God knows best. And His statement: And they whispered secretly means they whispered among themselves They said, ‘Indeed, these two are magicians’ This is the language of some Arabs, and this reading came with its syntactic analysis, and some of them read Indeed, these two are magicians and this is the well-known language, and grammarians have expanded in answering the first reading with what is not its place. The point is that the magicians said among themselves: You know that this man and his brother - meaning Moses and Aaron - are two learned magicians, experts in the art of magic, and they want on this day to defeat you and your people and take control of the people, and the common people will follow them, and they will fight Pharaoh and his soldiers, so they will be victorious over him, and they will expel you from your land. And his saying: And they will take away your best way meaning, and they will take over this way, which is magic, because they were respected because of it, and they had wealth and provisions based on it. They would say: If these two prevail, they will destroy you and expel you from the land, and they will be the only ones to do that and the leadership will be theirs without you. It was mentioned earlier in the hadith of the trials that Ibn Abbas said regarding his saying: And they will take away your best way meaning their kingdom that they are in and their livelihood. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Naim bin Hammad told us, Hisham told us on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq, he heard al-Sha’bi narrating on the authority of Ali regarding his saying: And they will take away your best way he said: They will turn people’s faces towards them. Mujahid said: And they will go with your best way. He said: Those with honor, intelligence, and age. Abu Salih said: With your best way are your nobles and leaders. Ikrimah said: With your best. Qatada said: “And their best way at that time was the Children of Israel, and they were the most numerous and wealthy of the people, so the enemy of God said: They want to go with it for themselves.” Abdurrahman bin Zaid said: With your best way is what you are on. “So assemble your plan, then come in ranks.” That is, all of you gather in one row, and throw what is in your hands at once to dazzle the eyes, and overcome this one and his brother. And he has succeeded today who has prevailed. That is, from us and from him. As for us, we have promised this king a generous gift, and as for him, he will attain great leadership.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Musayyab bin Wadh told us in Mecca, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, Al-Awza’i said: When the magicians fell down in prostration, Paradise was raised up for them so that they could look at it. He said: And it was mentioned on the authority of Saeed bin Salam, Ismail bin Abdullah bin Sulaiman told us on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, his statement: So the magicians fell down in prostration he said: They saw their houses being built for them while they were in their prostration, and this is what Ikrimah and Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza said.
20:70: God Almighty says, informing about the magicians when they agreed with Moses, peace be upon him, that they said to Moses, Either you throw meaning you are the first or we will be the first to throw * He said, Rather, throw meaning you are the first so that we may see what magic you will do, and so that the clear nature of their matter will be made clear to the people Then behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him from their magic as if they were moving and in another verse that when they threw, they said, 'By the might of Pharaoh, indeed we are the victors' and God Almighty said, They bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them and produced a great magic and He said here, Then behold, their ropes and staffs appeared to him from their magic as if they were moving" and that is because they put in them mercury which caused them to move and become disturbed and sway, so that it would seem to the observer that they were moving by their own choice, but it was only a trick, and they were a large crowd and a great group, so each of them threw a staff and a rope until the valley became full of snakes riding on each other. And His saying: So Moses felt fear within himself meaning he feared that the people would be tempted by their magic and be deceived by them before he threw what was in his right hand, so God Almighty revealed to him at that moment to throw what was in your right hand, meaning his staff, and behold it swallowed what they had made, and that was that it became a great, terrifying dragon with legs, a neck, a head and molars, so it began to follow those ropes and staffs until it did not leave anything of them except that it swallowed it and the magicians and the people were watching that clearly, openly, in broad daylight, so the miracle occurred and the proof became clear, and the truth occurred and the magic was nullified, and for this reason God Almighty said: They have only made a magician’s trick, and the magician will not succeed wherever he goes. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Shaibani told us, Hammad ibn Khalid told us, Ibn Muadh told us, I think it was al-Sayegh, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Jundub, on the authority of Abdullah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When you seize him, meaning the magician, then kill him. Then he recited: And he will not succeed. The magician wherever he came from said: He does not believe in him wherever he is found. Its origin was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi as a chain of transmission ending with him and as a chain of transmission ending with him. Then they fell down in prostration to God and said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron. Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza said: They were seventy thousand. Al-Suddi said: Thirty-some thousand. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abd Al-Aziz ibn Rafi’ on the authority of Abu Thamamah: The magicians of Pharaoh were nineteen thousand. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They were fifteen thousand. Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: They were twelve thousand. 20:71: The Almighty says, informing about Pharaoh's disbelief, stubbornness, transgression, and his opposition to truth with falsehood, when he saw what he saw of the dazzling miracle and the great sign, and saw that those whom he had sought for help had believed in the presence of all the people, and had been completely defeated, he began to be stubborn and slanderous, and turned to using his prestige and authority against the magicians, so he threatened them and warned them and said: You believed him meaning you believed him before I gave you permission meaning I did not command you to do that and you tempted me in that, and he said a statement that he and the magicians and all of creation knew was slander and a lie He is your leader who taught you magic meaning you only took magic from Moses, and you and him agreed against me and my subjects to make it appear, as the Almighty said in the other verse: This is indeed a plot which you plotted in the city to expel its people from it, and you are going to know, then he began to threaten them and said: "I will surely cut off your hands and your feet from I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, meaning, I will make you an example, I will kill you, and I will disgrace you. Ibn Abbas said: He was the first to do that. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. And His saying, And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting, meaning, you say, My people and I are in error, while you are with Moses and his people on guidance, so you will know who will have the punishment and will remain in it. So when he attacked them with that and threatened them, their souls became insignificant to them in God Almighty, and they said, ‘We will never prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs,’ meaning, we will never choose you over what we have obtained of guidance and certainty, and He who created us, it is possible that it is an oath, and it is possible that it is conjoined with the clear proofs, meaning, we will not choose you over our Creator and Maker who created us from nothingness, the Initiator, created us from clay, so He is the One who deserves worship and submission, not you, so decree what you will decree, meaning, do whatever you wish and whatever your hand reaches, you only decree this worldly life, meaning, you only have authority in this world, which is the world of transience, and we have desired the eternal home, indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins, meaning whatever we have done of Sins, especially what you forced us to do, which is regret, because it contradicts the verse of God Almighty and the miracle of His Prophet. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Naim bin Hammad told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And what you forced us to do of magic, he said: Pharaoh took forty boys from the Children of Israel and ordered them to learn magic in Pharma, and he said: Teach them a teaching that no one on earth knows. Ibn Abbas said: They are among those who believed in Moses and they are among those who said: We believe in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you forced us to do of magic. And Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said the same. And his statement: And God is better and more lasting means better for us than you, and more lasting meaning more lasting in reward than what you promised us and what you promised us, and this is a narration from Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him. Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi said: And God is better meaning more lasting in punishment than you if I obey, and more lasting meaning more lasting in punishment than you if I disobey, and something similar was narrated from Ibn Ishaq as well. It appears that Pharaoh - may God curse him - was determined to do that, and he did it to them out of mercy for them from God. That is why Ibn Abbas and others of the Salaf said: They became magicians in the morning and martyrs in the evening.

20:74: It appears from the context that this is part of what the magicians preached to Pharaoh, warning him of God’s vengeance and His everlasting and everlasting punishment, and encouraging him to attain His eternal and immortal reward. They said: Whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, meaning he meets God on the Day of Resurrection as a criminal, for him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live, like His statement: “It will not be decreed for them to die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful person.” And He said: And the most wretched will avoid it, who will enter the Great Fire, then he will neither die therein nor live. And God Almighty said: And they will cry, ‘O Malik, let your Lord decree upon us.’ He will say, ‘Indeed, you will remain.’ Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Ismail told us, Saeed ibn Yazid told us on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for the people of Hell who are its people, they will neither die therein nor live, but there are people who will be struck by the Fire because of their sins, so it will kill them. Death until they become charcoal. Then permission is given for intercession, and they are brought in groups, groups, and spread out on the rivers of Paradise. It is said: O people of Paradise, pour out rain upon them. So they grow like a seed that is in the silt of a torrent.” A man from the people said: It is as if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the desert. Muslim narrated it in this way in his Sahih book on the authority of Shu’bah and Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, both of them on the authority of Abu Salamah Sa’id ibn Yazid. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned on the authority of Abdul-Warith bin Abdul-Samad bin Abdul-Warith, who said: My father told us, Hayyan told us, I heard Sulayman al-Taymi on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Sa`id that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave a sermon and came to this verse: Whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “As for its people who are its people, they will neither die therein nor live. As for those who are not its people, the Fire will touch them, then the intercessors will arise and intercede, and the she-camels will be made, and they will be brought to a river called Life or Life, and they will grow as grass grows in the mud of a torrent.” And the Almighty said: And whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds meaning, and whoever meets his Lord on the Day of Resurrection with a believer in heart, having confirmed his conscience in his words and deeds, for those are the highest degrees meaning Paradise with its high degrees, secure rooms, and good dwellings. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Zaid bin Aslam told us, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Ubadah bin As-Samit, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Paradise has one hundred degrees, between every two degrees is like the distance between the heaven and the earth, and Al-Firdaws is the highest degree, and from it flow the four rivers, and the Throne is above it, so if you ask God for them, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws.” And Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Hammam, with the same chain. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi told us, Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Abi Malik told us on the authority of his father, who said: It was said: Paradise has one hundred levels, each level has a hundred levels, between every two levels is like the distance between the sky and the earth, in them are rubies and jewels, in each level there is a prince to whom they see virtue and leadership. In the two Sahihs it says: “The people of ‘Illiyyin will see those above them as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky, due to the difference between them. They said: O Messenger of God, those are the dwellings of the prophets. He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, men who believed in God and believed in the Messengers.” In the Sunan it says: Abu Bakr and ‘Umar were among them and were blessed. His statement: Gardens of Eden means residence, and it is a substitute for the highest levels. Beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein means remaining forever. And that is the reward of he who purifies himself means purifies himself from filth, evil, and polytheism, and worships God alone, with no partner. And follows the Messengers in what they brought of good and seeking.

God has elaborated on this matter in other than this noble surah, and that is because when Moses went out with the Children of Israel, they became without any of them in Egypt, neither a caller nor an answerer, so Pharaoh became very angry, and sent gatherers to the cities, meaning those who would gather soldiers for him from his countries and villages, saying: Indeed, these are a small group * And indeed, they are a source of anger to us. Then when he gathered his soldiers and his army was ready for him, he went in pursuit of them, so they followed them at sunrise, meaning at sunrise. So when the two hosts saw each other, meaning each group looked at the other, the companions of Moses said, ‘Indeed, we are surely overtaken.’ He said, ‘No, indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me.’ Moses stopped with the Children of Israel at sea in front of them, and Pharaoh was behind them, so at that time God inspired him, Then strike for them a dry path through the sea. So he struck the sea. With his staff, he said: Cleft for me by the permission of God, so it split and each part was like a great mountain, meaning a great mountain, then God sent the wind on the land of the sea and it blew it until it became dry land like the face of the earth, so that is why He said: Then strike for them a dry path in the sea, fearing no overtaking meaning from Pharaoh nor fearing meaning from the sea that your people would drown, then God the Almighty said: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, but there covered them from the sea meaning the sea that which covered them meaning that which is well-known and famous, and this is said in the case of a well-known and famous matter, as God the Almighty said: And the overturned land he inclined * So there covered it that which covered it and the poet said: I am the father of the star and my hair is my hair That is, the one who is known and famous. And just as Pharaoh preceded them and led them into the sea and led them astray and did not guide them to the path of righteousness, so will he precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and what an evil place they will be led to.

20:80: God Almighty mentions His great blessings and immense favors upon the Children of Israel, as He saved them from their enemy Pharaoh, and comforted their eyes from him while they watched him and his soldiers drown in one morning, and none of them escaped, as He said: And We drowned Pharaoh’s people while you were looking on. Al-Bukhari said: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Ruh bin Ubadah told us, Shu’bah told us, Abu Bishr told us on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, he found the Jews fasting on Ashura, so he asked them and they said: This is the day on which God gave Moses victory over Pharaoh, so he said: We are more deserving of Moses, so fast on it. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih. Then, after the destruction of Pharaoh, God Almighty promised Moses and the Children of Israel to be on the right side of the mountain, which is where God Almighty spoke to him, and asked for a vision, and gave him the Torah there. In the meantime, the Children of Israel worshipped the calf, as God Almighty will tell us shortly. As for the manna and quails, we have already discussed that in Surat Al-Baqarah and other surahs. Manna was a sweet that would descend upon them from the sky, and quail was a bird that would fall upon them, so they would take from it whatever they needed until the next day, out of God’s kindness, mercy, and goodness to them. For this reason, God Almighty said: Eat from the good things We have provided for you, and do not transgress therein, lest My wrath should descend upon you. That is, eat from this provision that I have provided you, and do not transgress therein, so that you take it without need, and disobey what I have commanded you, or My wrath should descend upon you, that is, I should become angry with you. And he upon whom My wrath descends has certainly perished. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: That is, he has become wretched. Shafi bin Mani’ said: There is a palace in Hell from which the unbeliever is thrown, and he falls into Hell for forty autumns before reaching the clay. This is what he said: And whoever incurs My wrath has certainly fallen. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. And His statement: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents, believes and does righteousness means whoever repents to Me, I will accept his repentance from whatever sin he may have committed, even to the extent that He accepted the repentance of those from the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf. And His statement: He repented means he turned back from what he was in of disbelief, polytheism, disobedience or hypocrisy. And His statement: And believed means in his heart. And did righteousness means with his limbs. And His statement: Then he was guided Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning then he did not doubt. And Saeed ibn Jubayr said: Then he was guided means he adhered to the Sunnah and the Jama’ah. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and more than one of the early Muslims. And Qatadah said: Then he was guided means he adhered to Islam until he died. And Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: Then he was guided means he knew that there was a reward for this, and then here is to arrange the report on the report, like His statement: But as for those who believed and did righteous deeds.

20:83: When Moses, peace be upon him, set out with the Children of Israel after the destruction of Pharaoh, "they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols. They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.' He said, 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. Indeed, what they are doing is ruined, and what they have been doing is futile.'" And his Lord promised him thirty nights, then He followed them with ten, so forty nights were completed, meaning that he fasted them night and day. This was explained in the hadith of the trials, so Moses, peace be upon him, hastened to the mountain, and he appointed his brother Aaron as his successor over the Children of Israel. For this reason, the Almighty said, And what made you leave your people, O Moses? He said, 'They are on my heels.' That is, they are coming and descending close to the mountain. And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased. That is, so that My pleasure may increase. He said, 'Indeed, We have tried your people after you, and the Samiri led them astray.' The Almighty informed His Prophet Moses of what happened after him among the Children of Israel and their worship of the calf that the Samiri made for them. In the Israelite books, his name was also Aaron, and God Almighty wrote for him during this period the tablets containing the Torah, as God Almighty said: “And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things. So take it with determination and command your people to take the best of it. I will show you the home of the wicked.” That is, the consequence of those who disobey Me and oppose My command. And His saying: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, meaning after God Almighty informed him of that, he was extremely angry and furious with them. He was concerned about their matter and received the Torah, which contained their law and honor for them. They were a people who worshipped other than God. No rational person with a mind and wisdom knows the falsehood of what they were doing and the foolishness of their minds and intellects. For this reason He said: He returned to them, angry and grieved. Grief is intense anger. Mujahid said: Ghadban with sorrow meaning angry. Qatada and As-Suddi said: He was sad and grieving over what his people did after him. “He said, ‘O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise?’” meaning, “Did He not promise you on my tongue every good thing in this world and the hereafter and a good end, as you witnessed of His victory over your enemy and your victory over him and other favors of God? “Has the covenant been prolonged for you?” meaning, in anticipation of what God promised you and forgetting what had passed of His blessings and what was in the covenant, Or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should descend upon you? “Or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should descend upon you?” Or did you desire that the wrath of your Lord should descend upon you? “So you broke your promise to Me.” The Children of Israel said in response to what Moses rebuked and rebuked them: We did not break your promise to you by our own power. That is, by our own power and choice. Then they began to make a cold excuse, telling him about their piety regarding the Coptic jewelry that they had in their hands, which they had borrowed from them when they were in Egypt. They left Egypt, so we threw it away. It was mentioned in the hadith of the tribulations that it was Aaron, peace be upon him, who ordered them to throw the jewelry into a pit in which there was fire. In the narration of al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Aaron wanted all the jewelry to be gathered in that pit and made into one stone, so that when Moses, peace be upon him, returned, he would see in it what he wanted. Then that Samaritan came and threw that handful that he had taken from the trace of the Messenger on it, and asked Aaron to ask God to answer his prayer. Aaron prayed for him, not knowing what he wanted, and he was answered. Then the Samaritan said: I ask God that it be a calf. So it was a calf that made a lowing sound, as a lure, a respite, a trial and a test. For this reason, he said: So the Samaritan threw * And brought out for them a calf, a body that made a lowing sound. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Ubadah bin Al-Najtari told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Harun passed by the Samaritan while he was carving a calf, and he said to him: What are you doing? He said: I am doing what is harmful and not beneficial. Harun said: O God, give him what he asked for, despite what is in his heart, and Harun went on. The Samaritan said: O God, I ask You to make Fakhar fall down, so when he fell down, they prostrated to him, and when he fell down, they raised their heads. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Hammad and said: I am doing what is beneficial and not harmful. Al-Suddi said: He was mooing and walking, so they said: Which of them were astray who were tempted by the calf and worshipped it: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot. That is, he forgot it here and went looking for it. This is what was mentioned previously in the hadith of the trials on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid said the same. Samak said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So he forgot, that is, he forgot to remind you that this is your god. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Hakim bin Jubayr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he said: This is your god and the god of Moses. He said: So they devoted themselves to it and loved it with a love they had never loved anything, meaning the like of it. God says: So he forgot, meaning he abandoned what he was upon of Islam, meaning the Samaritan. God the Almighty said in response to them, rebuking them, and explaining their disgrace and the foolishness of their minds in what they went to: Do they not see that it returns no word to them, nor does it possess for them any harm or benefit? That is, the calf. Do they not see that it does not answer them when they ask it or when they address it, nor does it possess for them any harm or benefit? That is, in their worldly life or in their afterlife? Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: No, by God, its mooing was nothing but the gas entering its anus. It comes out of its mouth and a sound is heard from it. It was mentioned earlier in the hadith of Al-Fitun on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that the name of this calf was Bahamut. The gist of what these ignorant people used as an excuse is that they were reluctant to wear the adornments of the Copts, so they threw them away and worshipped the calf. They were reluctant to do something insignificant and did something major, as came in the authentic hadith on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that a man from Iraq asked him about the blood of a mosquito if it got on a garment, meaning should one pray in it or not? Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, said: Look at the people of Iraq. They killed the son of the daughter of the Messenger of God, meaning Al-Hussein, and they are asking about the blood of a mosquito.

It was mentioned in the hadith of the tribulations that it was Aaron, peace be upon him, who ordered them to throw the jewelry into a pit in which there was fire. In the narration of al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Aaron wanted all the jewelry to be gathered in that pit and made into one stone, so that when Moses, peace be upon him, returned, he would see in it what he wanted. Then that Samaritan came and threw that handful that he had taken from the trace of the Messenger on it, and asked Aaron to ask God to answer his prayer. Aaron prayed for him, not knowing what he wanted, and he was answered. Then the Samaritan said: I ask God that it be a calf. So it was a calf that made a lowing sound, as a lure, a respite, a trial and a test. For this reason, he said: So the Samaritan threw * And brought out for them a calf, a body that made a lowing sound. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Ubadah bin Al-Najtari told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Harun passed by the Samaritan while he was carving a calf, and he said to him: What are you doing? He said: I am doing what is harmful and not beneficial. Harun said: O God, give him what he asked for, despite what is in his heart, and Harun went on. The Samaritan said: O God, I ask You to make Fakhar fall down, so when he fell down, they prostrated to him, and when he fell down, they raised their heads. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Hammad and said: I am doing what is beneficial and not harmful. Al-Suddi said: He was mooing and walking, so they said: Which of them were astray who were tempted by the calf and worshipped it: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot. That is, he forgot it here and went looking for it. This is what was mentioned previously in the hadith of the trials on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid said the same. Samak said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So he forgot, that is, he forgot to remind you that this is your god. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Hakim bin Jubayr on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, so he said: This is your god and the god of Moses. He said: So they devoted themselves to it and loved it with a love they had never loved anything, meaning the like of it. God says: So he forgot, meaning he abandoned what he was upon of Islam, meaning the Samaritan. God the Almighty said in response to them, rebuking them, and explaining their disgrace and the foolishness of their minds in what they went to: Do they not see that it returns no word to them, nor does it possess for them any harm or benefit? That is, the calf. Do they not see that it does not answer them when they ask it or when they address it, nor does it possess for them any harm or benefit? That is, in their worldly life or in their afterlife? Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: No, by God, its mooing was nothing but the gas entering its anus. It comes out of its mouth and a sound is heard from it. It was mentioned earlier in the hadith of Al-Fitun on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that the name of this calf was Bahamut. The gist of what these ignorant people used as an excuse is that they were reluctant to wear the adornments of the Copts, so they threw them away and worshipped the calf. They were reluctant to do something insignificant and did something major, as came in the authentic hadith on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that a man from Iraq asked him about the blood of a mosquito if it got on a garment, meaning should one pray in it or not? Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, said: Look at the people of Iraq. They killed the son of the daughter of the Messenger of God, meaning Al-Hussein, and they are asking about the blood of a mosquito.
20:90: The Almighty tells us about what happened when Aaron, peace be upon him, forbade them from worshipping the calf and told them, “This is only a trial for you, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, who created everything and determined it with [precise] determination, the Possessor of the Glorious Throne, the Doer of whatever He wills. “So follow me and obey my command,” meaning in what I command you to do, and leave what I forbid you from doing. They said, ‘We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us,’ meaning we will not leave its worship until we hear Moses’ words about it. They opposed Aaron in that and fought him and almost killed him.

20:92: God Almighty tells about Moses, peace be upon him, when he returned to his people and saw what had happened to them of the great matter, so he was filled with anger and threw down what was in his hand of the divine tablets, and grabbed his brother's head, dragging him towards him. We have already explained this in detail in Surat Al-A'raf, and we mentioned there the hadith "Hearing is not like seeing." And he began to blame his brother Aaron, so he said: "What prevented you when you saw them go astray * That you did not follow meaning that you inform me of this matter when it first happened Did you disobey my command" meaning in what I had presented to you, which is His saying: "Take my place among my people and do good and do not follow the way of the corrupters He said, O son of my mother" He was softening him by mentioning the mother even though he was his brother from both parents, because mentioning the mother here is more tender and more eloquent in tenderness and affection, and for this reason he said: "O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head" the verse, this is an apology from Aaron to Moses for the reason for his delay from him as he did not catch up with him to inform him of what had happened of this matter The body said: I feared that I would follow you and tell you this, and you would say to me, Why did you leave them alone and separate them? “And did you not observe my word?” That is, and did you not observe what I commanded you to do when I appointed you as their successor. Ibn Abbas said: And Aaron was fearful and obedient to him.

20:95: Moses, peace be upon him, said to the Samaritan: What made you do what you did? What happened to you that you did what you did? Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Hakim bin Jubair, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Samaritan was a man from the people of Bajarma, and he was from a people who worshipped cows, and he loved worshipping cows in his soul, and he had declared Islam with the Children of Israel, and his name was Musa bin Thafar, and in a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas it is said that he was from Kerman, and Qatada said: He was from the village of Samarra. He said, I saw what they did not see, meaning I saw Gabriel when he came to destroy Pharaoh, and I took a handful of the Messenger’s trace, meaning the trace of his horse, and this is the well-known view among many or most of the commentators. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn al-Harith told us, Ubayd God ibn Musa told me, Israel told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abi ibn Ammarah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and took Moses, peace be upon him, up to heaven, the Samaritan saw him from among the people, so he grabbed a handful of the horse’s mark. He said: Gabriel carried Moses, peace be upon them both, behind him until he approached the gate of heaven, he ascended and God wrote the tablets, and he heard the creaking of the pens on the tablets. When he informed him that his people had been tempted after him, he said: Moses descended, took the calf and burned it. Strange. Mujahid said: So I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger. He said: From under the hoof of Gabriel’s horse. He said: A handful is the size of a palm, and a handful is the tips of the fingers. Mujahid said: The Samaritan threw what was in his hand onto the ornaments of the Children of Israel, and it formed a calf with a body that had a lowing sound, the rustling of the wind in it, so it made it low. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Yahya told us, Ali bin Al-Madini told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Amara told us, Ikrimah told us that the Samaritan saw the Messenger, and it was cast into his mind that if you took a handful from the footprint of this horse and threw it into something and said to it, Be, then it was. So he took a handful from the footprint of the Messenger, and his fingers dried up on the handful. When Moses went to the appointed time, and the Children of Israel had borrowed the jewelry of the people of Pharaoh, the Samaritan said to them: It only happened to you because of this jewelry, so gather it. So they gathered it and lit a fire over it and it melted. The Samaritan saw it and it was cast into his mind that if you threw this handful into this and said, Be, then it was. So he threw the handful and said, Be, and it was a calf with a body that mooed. So he said, This is your god and the god of Moses. That is why he said, So I threw it, meaning I threw it with whomever I threw it. And thus my soul enticed me, meaning it made it good and pleased me. At that time, He said, ‘Then go, for in life you will have the ability to say, ‘No.’ Touching” means just as you took and touched what you were not allowed to take or touch from the trace of the Messenger, then your punishment in this world is that you say no touching, meaning do not touch people and they will not touch you. And indeed, you have an appointment, meaning the Day of Resurrection, that you will not fail to fulfill, meaning you will have no escape from it. Qatada said, that you say “no touching, meaning: A punishment for them and their remnants today, who say no touching. And His statement: And indeed, you have an appointment which you will not fail to keep. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abu Nahik said: You will not be absent from it. And His statement: And look at your god, meaning your object of worship, to which you have been devoted, meaning you have continued to worship it, meaning the calf. We will burn it. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi: He dragged it with a file and threw it into the fire. Qatadah said: The calf was transformed from gold into flesh and blood, so he burned it with fire, then threw its ashes into the sea. That is why He said: Then We will scatter it into the sea, a blast. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Raja told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ammarah bin Abd and Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When Moses hastened to his Lord, the Samaritan gathered what he could of the jewelry of the women of the Children of Israel, then he made it into a calf. Moses went to the calf and put the files on it, and he cooled it with them while he was on the bank of a river. No one who used to worship the calf drank from that water except that his face turned yellow like gold. They said to Moses: What is our repentance? He said: Some of you will kill one another. And this is what al-Suddi said, and it was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of Surat al-Baqarah, then in the hadith of the trials he elaborated on that. And the Almighty says: “Your god is only God, other than whom there is no god. He encompasses all things in knowledge.” Moses, peace be upon him, says to them: This is not your god. Your god is only God, other than whom there is no god. And worship is due only to Him, for everything is in need of Him and is a slave to Him. And His saying: He encompasses all things in knowledge is in the accusative case of specification, meaning He is All-Knowing of everything. He encompasses all things in knowledge, and He has counted all things in number, so not an atom’s weight escapes Him. “Not a leaf falls but He knows it. And there is no grain within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is [written] in a clear register.” “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.” And the verses on this are very many.

That is why he said, So I threw it, meaning I threw it with whomever I threw it. And thus my soul enticed me, meaning it made it good and pleased me. At that time, He said, ‘Then go, for in life you will have the ability to say, ‘No.’ Touching” means just as you took and touched what you were not allowed to take or touch from the trace of the Messenger, then your punishment in this world is that you say no touching, meaning do not touch people and they will not touch you. And indeed, you have an appointment, meaning the Day of Resurrection, that you will not fail to fulfill, meaning you will have no escape from it. Qatada said, that you say “no touching, meaning: A punishment for them and their remnants today, who say no touching. And His statement: And indeed, you have an appointment which you will not fail to keep. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abu Nahik said: You will not be absent from it. And His statement: And look at your god, meaning your object of worship, to which you have been devoted, meaning you have continued to worship it, meaning the calf. We will burn it. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi: He dragged it with a file and threw it into the fire. Qatadah said: The calf was transformed from gold into flesh and blood, so he burned it with fire, then threw its ashes into the sea. That is why He said: Then We will scatter it into the sea, a blast. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Raja told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Ammarah bin Abd and Abu Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When Moses hastened to his Lord, the Samaritan gathered what he could of the jewelry of the women of the Children of Israel, then he made it into a calf. Moses went to the calf and put the files on it, and he cooled it with them while he was on the bank of a river. No one who used to worship the calf drank from that water except that his face turned yellow like gold. They said to Moses: What is our repentance? He said: Some of you will kill one another. And this is what al-Suddi said, and it was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of Surat al-Baqarah, then in the hadith of the trials he elaborated on that. And the Almighty says: “Your god is only God, other than whom there is no god. He encompasses all things in knowledge.” Moses, peace be upon him, says to them: This is not your god. Your god is only God, other than whom there is no god. And worship is due only to Him, for everything is in need of Him and is a slave to Him. And His saying: He encompasses all things in knowledge is in the accusative case of specification, meaning He is All-Knowing of everything. He encompasses all things in knowledge, and He has counted all things in number, so not an atom’s weight escapes Him. “Not a leaf falls but He knows it. And there is no grain within the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is [written] in a clear register.” “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.” And the verses on this are very many.
20:99: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Just as We related to you the story of Moses and what happened to him with Pharaoh and his soldiers in plain terms and as a reality, so do We relate to you the past stories as they occurred, without addition or subtraction. This is what We have given you from Us, that is, from Us, a reminder, which is the great Qur’an that falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it, a revelation from the Wise, the Praiseworthy, who has not given any prophet from the prophets since they were sent until they were sealed with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a book like it, nor more complete than it, nor more comprehensive of the report of what came before and the report of what will be, and the judgment of judgment between people from it. That is why God the Almighty said: Whoever turns away from it meaning, denies it and turns away from following its commands and requests, and seeks guidance from someone other than it, then God will misguide him and guide him to the lowest part of Hell. That is why He said: Whoever turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection meaning a sin, as God the Almighty said: And whoever disbelieves in it from the parties, the Fire will be his promised destination. This is general for everyone to whom the Qur’an has reached, from the Arabs and non-Arabs, the People of the Book and others, as He said: That I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. So everyone to whom the Qur’an has reached, it is a warner and a farewell. Whoever follows it will be guided, and whoever opposes it and turns away from it will go astray and be wretched in this world, and Hell will be his promised destination on the Day of Resurrection. That is why He said: Whoever turns away from it will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection, abiding eternally therein meaning, they will have no escape from it or escape. And evil will be their burden on the Day of Resurrection meaning, what an evil burden they will bear.

20:102: It was proven in the hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the trumpet, and he said: A horn that will be blown. It was mentioned in the hadith of the trumpet on the authority of Abu Hurairah that it is a great horn, the circle of which is the size of the heavens and the earth, and Israfil, peace be upon him, will blow into it. It was mentioned in the hadith: How can I enjoy myself while the owner of the trumpet has taken hold of the trumpet and bowed his forehead, and is waiting for permission to be given to him? They said: O Messenger of God, what should we say? He said: Say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust." And His saying: And We shall gather the criminals on that Day blue-eyed It was said: Its meaning is blue-eyed from the intensity of the horrors they are in. They whisper among themselves. Ibn Abbas said: They whisper among themselves, meaning some of them say to each other: You have only remained ten meaning in this worldly abode. Your stay in it was short, ten days or so. God the Most High said: We know best what they say meaning in the state of their whispering among themselves When the best of them in conduct says meaning the most rational and complete among them You have only remained a day meaning because the duration of this world is short in their minds on the Day of Resurrection, because the entire world, even if its times are repeated and its nights, days and hours follow one another, is as if it were one day. For this reason the disbelievers shorten the duration of worldly life on the Day of Resurrection, and their purpose in that was to prevent the argument from being established against them because of the short duration. For this reason God the Most High said: “And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear that they had not remained except for an hour. Thus were they deluded. And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, “Indeed, you have remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.” So this is the Day of Resurrection, but you did not know.” And He said: God Almighty said: Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember, and a warner came to you? The verse. God Almighty also said: How many years did you remain on the earth? They said, “We remained a day or part of a day, so ask the counters. He said, You remained only a little, if you only knew. That is, your stay on it was only a little. If you only knew, you would have preferred the everlasting over the transient, but you acted in a bad way. You preferred the present transient over the everlasting.

20:105: God Almighty says: And they ask you about the mountains, meaning will they remain on the Day of Resurrection or will they disappear? “Say, ‘My Lord will blow it away with a blast,’ meaning He will sweep it away from its place, obliterate it, and disperse it, ‘and leave it,’ meaning the earth, ‘a flat plain,’ meaning a single carpet. A flat plain is a confirmation of the meaning of that, and it was said that which has no vegetation in it. The first is more appropriate, although the second is also intended by the intransitive. That is why He said, ‘You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness,’ meaning you will not see on the earth on that day any valley or hill, nor any low or high place. This is what Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and more than one of the early Muslims said. ‘On that Day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness in him,’ meaning on the day they see these conditions and terrors, they will respond quickly to the Caller, wherever they are commanded, they will hasten to him. If this had been in this world, it would have been more beneficial for them, but it will not benefit them, as God Almighty said, ‘I will hear of them and see them on the Day they come to Us,’ and He said, ‘Rushing to the Caller.’ Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: God will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in Darkness, the sky is folded up, the stars are scattered, the sun and moon go, and a caller calls out, and the people follow the voice, and that is His statement: “On that Day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness in him.” Qatada said: With no crookedness in him, meaning they will not deviate from him. Abu Salih said: With no crookedness in him, meaning with no crookedness from him. And his saying: And the voices are humbled before the Most Gracious, Ibn Abbas said: They are still. Al-Suddi said the same. So you will not hear anything but a whisper, Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means the trampling of feet. And this is what Ikrimah, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others said. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So you will not hear anything but a whisper, the low voice, and this is a narration on the authority of Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak. Saeed bin Jubair said: So you will not hear anything but a whisper, the hadith and its secret and the trampling of feet, Saeed combined both sayings, and it is possible. As for the trampling of feet, what is meant is the people’s striving towards the place of gathering, which is their walking in stillness and submission. As for the low speech, it may be in one situation and not another, as God the Almighty said: “On the Day He comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. So among them will be the wretched and the blessed.”

20:109: God Almighty says: On that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection no intercession will benefit meaning with Him except for one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission and whose word He is pleased with like His saying: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? and His saying: And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after God has given permission to whom He wills and is pleased with. And He said: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased, and they are fearful for His fear. And He said: And intercession will not benefit with Him except for one to whom He has given permission. And He said: On the Day the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except for one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission and who says what is right. In the two Sahihs, from more than one source, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is the master of the children of Adam and the most honorable of creation in the sight of God, the Almighty, he said, “I will come beneath the Throne, and I will prostrate before God, and He will open up to me with praises that I cannot count now, and He will leave me as long as He wills to leave me, then He will say, ‘O Muhammad, raise your head and say, and you will be heard, and intercede and your intercession will be accepted. ’ Then He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise, then I will return.” He mentioned this four times, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him and upon all the prophets. In the hadith also, “God the Almighty says, ‘Bring out from the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith,’ so they will bring out many people, then He will say, ‘Bring out from the Fire whoever has in his heart half a weight of faith, bring out from the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of an atom, whoever has in his heart the smallest, smallest weight of an atom of faith. ’” And His statement: He knows what is before them and what is behind them means He encompasses all of creation with His knowledge, but they do not encompass Him with His knowledge like His statement: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. And His statement: And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining Ibn Abbas and others said: The creations will submit, humble themselves, and surrender to their Almighty, the Ever-Living who does not die, the Self-Sustaining who does not sleep, and He is the Guardian of everything that He manages and preserves, for He is the Perfect in Himself, to whom everything is in need and has no sustenance except through Him. And His statement: And he who bears injustice will fail means on the Day of Resurrection, for God will render every right to its owner until He takes revenge for the hornless sheep from the horned sheep. And in the hadith: “God the Almighty says: By My glory and majesty, no injustice of an oppressor will surpass Me today.” And in the Sahih: “Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection, and the complete disappointment is for he who meets God while associating partners with Him, for God the Almighty says: Indeed, associating partners with God is a great injustice.” And His statement: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will not fear injustice or deprivation, when He mentioned the wrongdoers and their threat, He followed it with the righteous and their ruling, which is that they will not be wronged or deprived, meaning that their bad deeds will not be increased nor their good deeds decreased, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and more than one said. And He said: And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased, and they are fearful for His fear. 20:113: God Almighty says: And since the Day of Resurrection and the recompense for good and evil will inevitably come to pass, We sent down the Qur’an as a bringer of good tidings and a warner in clear, fluent Arabic, without ambiguity or defect, And We diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they might fear God meaning that they might abandon sins, forbidden acts, and indecencies or that it might cause them to remember meaning that they might establish obedience and perform acts of worship. So exalted is God, the True King meaning that the True King, Who is True, is exalted and sanctified, and His promise is True, and His threat is True, and His Messengers are True, and Paradise is True, and Hell is True, and everything from Him is True. His justice, the Almighty, is that He will not punish anyone before warning and sending the Messengers, and giving an excuse to His creation so that no one will have an excuse or doubt. And His saying: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before its revelation is completed to you, is like the saying of the Most High in Surat La Aqsam bi Yawm al-Qiyamah 75:“Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. And when we have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then indeed, upon Us is its clarification.” It was established in Sahih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was dealing with the severity of the revelation, and among the things he would move his tongue with was that God revealed this verse, meaning that whenever Gabriel came to him with the revelation, whenever Gabriel said a verse, he would say it with him out of his intense eagerness to memorize the Qur’an. So God, the Most High, guided him to what was easiest and lightest for him so that it would not be difficult for him, so He said: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation,” meaning that We will collect it in your chest, then you will recite it to the people without forgetting anything of it. “And when we have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then indeed, upon Us is its clarification.” And He said in this verse: And do not hasten with the Qur’an before it is completed to you. And his revelation” meaning listen, and when the angel has finished reading it to you, then read it after him, And say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge’ meaning increase me in knowledge from You. Ibn Uyaynah, may God have mercy on him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to increase until God Almighty took him, and for this reason it was stated in the hadith: “God continued the revelation to His Messenger, until the revelation was more than it was on the day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died.” Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Thabit, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: O God, benefit me with what You have taught me, and teach me what will benefit me, and increase me in knowledge, and praise be to God in every situation. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Numayr. He said: It is strange from this aspect, and Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Amr bin Ali Al-Fallas, on the authority of Abu Asim, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, with it, and he added at the end of it: And I seek refuge in God from the state of the people of Hell.

20:115: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Asbat bin Muhammad told us, Al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He was called human because he was entrusted with something and then forgot. And Ali bin Abi Talha narrated it likewise on his authority. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: He left. And His saying: And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ God Almighty mentions the honor and respect He bestowed upon Adam and the favor He bestowed upon him over many of those He created. We have already discussed this story in Surat Al-Baqarah, Al-A’raf, Al-Hijr, and Al-Kahf. It will come at the end of Surat Sad, where God Almighty mentions the creation of Adam and His command to the angels to prostrate to him as an honor and a sign of respect. He explains the enmity of Satan toward the children of Adam and their father in the past. For this reason God Almighty said: “So they prostrated, except Satan. He refused,” meaning he refused and was arrogant. “So We said, ‘O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife,’ meaning Eve, peace be upon them both. “So let him not expel you from Paradise and you become miserable.” That is, beware of striving to expel you from it and you become tired, troubled, and miserable in seeking your provision, for you are here in a comfortable and pleasant life without cost or difficulty. You shall not be hungry therein nor naked therein, He only linked hunger and nakedness because hunger is the humiliation of the inner self, and nakedness is the humiliation of the outer self. And you shall not be thirsty therein nor shall you be thirsty therein nor shall you be thirsty therein. The forenoon These two are also opposites, as thirst is the inner heat, which is thirst, and forenoon is the outer heat. And his saying: Then Satan whispered to him, saying, ‘O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not decay?’ It was previously mentioned that he guided them with deception. And he swore to them, ‘Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers.’ It was previously mentioned that God Almighty commanded Adam and his wife to eat from all the fruits and not to approach this specific tree in Paradise. Satan kept on pestering them until they ate from it, and it was the tree of eternity, meaning that whoever eats from it will be immortal and his stay will last a long time. The mention of the tree of eternity came in the hadith, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu al-Dahhak, I heard Abu Hurayrah narrating on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for a hundred years without crossing it, and it is the tree of eternity. Imam Ahmad narrated it. And his saying: So they ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created Adam as a tall man with much hair on his head, like a ripe palm tree. When he tasted the tree, his clothing fell off him, and the first thing that became apparent was his private parts. When he looked at his private parts, he began to struggle in Paradise, and a tree took hold of his hair, and he struggled with it. Then the Most Merciful called out to him: ‘O Adam, do you flee from Me?’ When he heard the words of the Most Merciful, he said: ‘O Lord, no, but out of shyness. What do you think if I repent and return, will I return to Paradise?’ He said: ‘Yes.’” So that is his saying: Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. This is a disconnected chain of transmission between al-Hasan and Ubayy ibn Ka`b, so he did not hear it from him, and there is also a problem with its being attributed to the Prophet. And His statement: And they began to patch together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise. Mujahid said: They patched together like a garment. Qatada and As-Suddi said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja`far ibn `Awn told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they began to patch together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise. He said: They would remove fig leaves and place them on their private parts. And his saying: “And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him.” Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah told us, Ayoub ibn al-Najjar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Moses argued with Adam, and he said to him: Are you the one who expelled the people from Paradise because of your sin and made them miserable? Adam said: O Moses, you are the one whom God chose with His messages and His speech. Do you blame me for something that God wrote for me before He created me or that God decreed for me before He created me? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So Adam argued with Moses.” This hadith has chains of transmission in the two Sahihs and other Musnads. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Anas bin Ayyad told me on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abi Dhi’ab, on the authority of Yazid bin Hormuz, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Adam and Moses argued before their Lord, and Adam argued with Moses. Moses said: ‘You are the one whom God created with His hand, and breathed into you of His spirit, and to whom His angels prostrated, and whom He settled in His Paradise, then you sent people down to the earth because of your sin.’ Adam said: ‘You are Moses whom God chose with His message and speech, and gave you the tablets in which everything is explained, and brought you near as a confidant. How long did you find God writing the Torah before I was created?’ Moses said: ‘Forty years.’ Adam said: ‘Did you find in it that Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Do you blame me for doing a deed that God had decreed for me to do forty years before He created me?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘So Adam argued with Moses.’” Al-Harith said: And Abd al-Rahman ibn Hormuz told me this on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

Satan kept on pestering them until they ate from it, and it was the tree of eternity, meaning that whoever eats from it will be immortal and his stay will last a long time. The mention of the tree of eternity came in the hadith, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah told us on the authority of Abu al-Dahhak, I heard Abu Hurayrah narrating on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider can travel for a hundred years without crossing it, and it is the tree of eternity. Imam Ahmad narrated it. And his saying: So they ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab told us, Ali ibn Asim told us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka`b, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God created Adam as a tall man with much hair on his head, like a ripe palm tree. When he tasted the tree, his clothing fell off him, and the first thing that became apparent was his private parts. When he looked at his private parts, he began to struggle in Paradise, and a tree took hold of his hair, and he struggled with it. Then the Most Merciful called out to him: ‘O Adam, do you flee from Me?’ When he heard the words of the Most Merciful, he said: ‘O Lord, no, but out of shyness. What do you think if I repent and return, will I return to Paradise?’ He said: ‘Yes.’” So that is his saying: Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance. This is a disconnected chain of transmission between al-Hasan and Ubayy ibn Ka`b, so he did not hear it from him, and there is also a problem with its being attributed to the Prophet. And His statement: And they began to patch together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise. Mujahid said: They patched together like a garment. Qatada and As-Suddi said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja`far ibn `Awn told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they began to patch together, over themselves, from the leaves of Paradise. He said: They would remove fig leaves and place them on their private parts. And his saying: “And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him.” Al-Bukhari said: Qutaybah told us, Ayoub ibn al-Najjar told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Moses argued with Adam, and he said to him: Are you the one who expelled the people from Paradise because of your sin and made them miserable? Adam said: O Moses, you are the one whom God chose with His messages and His speech. Do you blame me for something that God wrote for me before He created me or that God decreed for me before He created me? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So Adam argued with Moses.” This hadith has chains of transmission in the two Sahihs and other Musnads. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Anas bin Ayyad told me on the authority of Al-Harith bin Abi Dhi’ab, on the authority of Yazid bin Hormuz, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Adam and Moses argued before their Lord, and Adam argued with Moses. Moses said: ‘You are the one whom God created with His hand, and breathed into you of His spirit, and to whom His angels prostrated, and whom He settled in His Paradise, then you sent people down to the earth because of your sin.’ Adam said: ‘You are Moses whom God chose with His message and speech, and gave you the tablets in which everything is explained, and brought you near as a confidant. How long did you find God writing the Torah before I was created?’ Moses said: ‘Forty years.’ Adam said: ‘Did you find in it that Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray?’ He said: ‘Yes.’ He said: ‘Do you blame me for doing a deed that God had decreed for me to do forty years before He created me?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘So Adam argued with Moses.’” Al-Harith said: And Abd al-Rahman ibn Hormuz told me this on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
20:122: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Asbat bin Muhammad told us, Al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He was called human because he was entrusted with something and then forgot. And Ali bin Abi Talha narrated it likewise on his authority. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: He left. And His saying: And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ God Almighty mentions the honor and respect He bestowed upon Adam and the favor He bestowed upon him over many of those He created. We have already discussed this story in Surat Al-Baqarah, Al-A’raf, Al-Hijr, and Al-Kahf. It will come at the end of Surat Sad, where God Almighty mentions the creation of Adam and His command to the angels to prostrate to him as an honor and a sign of respect. He explains the enmity of Satan toward the children of Adam and their father in the past. For this reason God Almighty said: “So they prostrated, except Satan. He refused,” meaning he refused and was arrogant. “So We said, ‘O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife,’ meaning Eve, peace be upon them both. “So let him not expel you from Paradise and you become miserable.” That is, beware of striving to expel you from it and you become tired, troubled, and miserable in seeking your provision, for you are here in a comfortable and pleasant life without cost or difficulty. You shall not be hungry therein nor naked therein, He only linked hunger and nakedness because hunger is the humiliation of the inner self, and nakedness is the humiliation of the outer self. And you shall not be thirsty therein nor shall you be thirsty therein nor shall you be thirsty therein. The forenoon These two are also opposites, as thirst is the inner heat, which is thirst, and forenoon is the outer heat.
