20:123: God Almighty says to Adam, Eve, and Satan: Descend from it, all of you, meaning from Paradise, all of you. We have explained this in detail in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Some of you are enemies to others. He said: Adam and his offspring, and Satan and his offspring. And His statement: If there comes to you guidance from Me, Abu Al-Aaliyah said: the prophets, messengers and explanation. So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be miserable, Ibn Abbas said: he will neither go astray in this world nor be miserable in the Hereafter. And whoever turns away from My remembrance, meaning he disobeys My command and what I revealed to My Messenger, he turns away from it and forgets it and takes his guidance from someone other than Him. Surely he will have a depressed life, meaning a depressed life, so he will have no peace of mind and no expansion in his chest, rather his chest is tight and constricted because of his misguidance. Even if he appears to be comfortable and wears whatever he wants and eats whatever he wants and lives wherever he wants, his heart, as long as it does not reach certainty and guidance, is in anxiety, confusion and doubt. He will not cease to be in doubt and hesitate, and this is from the hardship of life. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For he will have a difficult life, meaning misery. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For he will have a difficult life, meaning: Whenever I give to one of My servants, whether little or much, and he does not fear Me in it, then there is no good in it, and it is the difficulty of living. He also said: There are misguided people who turned away from the truth and were in abundance in this world, being arrogant, so their life was difficult, because they thought that God would not replace their livelihoods due to their bad opinion of God and their denial. So if the servant denies God and has bad opinion of Him and trusts Him, then his life will be difficult for him, and that is the difficulty. Ad-Dahhak said: It is bad work and evil provision, and this is what Ikrimah and Malik bin Dinar said. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said on the authority of Abu Hazim on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Saeed regarding his statement: A straitened life, he said: His grave will be so narrow for him that his ribs will overlap in it. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: An-Nu’man ibn Abi Ayyash was called Abu Salamah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, al-Walid told us, Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Diraj on the authority of Abu al-Haitham on the authority of Abu Saeed who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding God Almighty’s statement: Then he will have a straitened life, he said: The grave will be squeezed for him. The suspended version is more authentic. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Asad bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj Abu Al-Samh told us, on the authority of Ibn Hujaira, whose name is Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The believer in his grave is in a green garden, and his grave is expanded for him by seventy cubits, and his grave is illuminated for him like the moon on a full moon night. Do you know why this verse was revealed: ‘For him is a miserable life.’ Do you know what a miserable life is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: The punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, ninety-nine dragons are set upon him. Do you know what a dragon is? Ninety-nine snakes, each snake has seven heads. They blow into his body and sting and scratch him until the Day of Resurrection.” Its chain of transmission is very strange. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi told us: Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Hisham ibn Saad told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Ibn Hijra, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Then he will have a miserable life. He said: The miserable life about which God said that ninety-nine snakes will be set upon him, which will devour his flesh until the Hour comes. He also said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abu al-Walid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then he will have a miserable life. He said: The torment of the grave. A good chain of transmission. And his saying: And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. Mujahid, Abu Salih, and As-Suddi said: There is no proof for him. Ikrimah said: Everything will be blind to him except Hell. It is possible that what is meant is that he will be resurrected or gathered to Hell blind in sight and insight as well, as God Almighty said: “And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their refuge will be Hell.” This is why he says: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind while I was seeing? That is, in this world. “He will say: ‘Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them. And thus today you will be forgotten.’” That is, when you turned away from the signs of God and treated them as one who did not remember them after they were conveyed to you, you forgot them, turned away from them, and neglected them. Thus today We will treat you as one who forgets you. So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. For the reward is of the same kind as the action. As for forgetting the wording of the Qur’an while understanding its meaning and carrying out its requirements, it is not included in this specific threat, even though it is threatened from another aspect, because the Sunnah has come with a definite prohibition and a severe threat in this regard. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Waleed told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of ‘Isa ibn Fa’id, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no man who recites the Qur’an and then forgets it except that he will meet God on the Day of Resurrection as a leper. Then Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of ‘Isa ibn Fa’id, on the authority of ‘Ubadah ibn as-Samit, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar.

As for forgetting the wording of the Qur’an while understanding its meaning and carrying out its requirements, it is not included in this specific threat, even though it is threatened from another aspect, because the Sunnah has come with a definite prohibition and a severe threat in this regard. Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Waleed told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of ‘Isa ibn Fa’id, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Sa’d ibn ‘Ubadah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no man who recites the Qur’an and then forgets it except that he will meet God on the Day of Resurrection as a leper. Then Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of ‘Isa ibn Fa’id, on the authority of ‘Ubadah ibn as-Samit, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar.
20:126: God Almighty says to Adam, Eve, and Satan: Descend from it, all of you, meaning from Paradise, all of you. We have explained this in detail in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Some of you are enemies to others. He said: Adam and his offspring, and Satan and his offspring. And His statement: If there comes to you guidance from Me, Abu Al-Aaliyah said: the prophets, messengers and explanation. So whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be miserable, Ibn Abbas said: he will neither go astray in this world nor be miserable in the Hereafter. And whoever turns away from My remembrance, meaning he disobeys My command and what I revealed to My Messenger, he turns away from it and forgets it and takes his guidance from someone other than Him. Surely he will have a depressed life, meaning a depressed life, so he will have no peace of mind and no expansion in his chest, rather his chest is tight and constricted because of his misguidance. Even if he appears to be comfortable and wears whatever he wants and eats whatever he wants and lives wherever he wants, his heart, as long as it does not reach certainty and guidance, is in anxiety, confusion and doubt. He will not cease to be in doubt and hesitate, and this is from the hardship of life. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For he will have a difficult life, meaning misery. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For he will have a difficult life, meaning: Whenever I give to one of My servants, whether little or much, and he does not fear Me in it, then there is no good in it, and it is the difficulty of living. He also said: There are misguided people who turned away from the truth and were in abundance in this world, being arrogant, so their life was difficult, because they thought that God would not replace their livelihoods due to their bad opinion of God and their denial. So if the servant denies God and has bad opinion of Him and trusts Him, then his life will be difficult for him, and that is the difficulty. Ad-Dahhak said: It is bad work and evil provision, and this is what Ikrimah and Malik bin Dinar said. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said on the authority of Abu Hazim on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Saeed regarding his statement: A straitened life, he said: His grave will be so narrow for him that his ribs will overlap in it. Abu Hatim al-Razi said: An-Nu’man ibn Abi Ayyash was called Abu Salamah. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Safwan told us, al-Walid told us, Abdullah ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Diraj on the authority of Abu al-Haitham on the authority of Abu Saeed who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding God Almighty’s statement: Then he will have a straitened life, he said: The grave will be squeezed for him. The suspended version is more authentic. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman told us, Asad bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj Abu Al-Samh told us, on the authority of Ibn Hujaira, whose name is Abd Al-Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The believer in his grave is in a green garden, and his grave is expanded for him by seventy cubits, and his grave is illuminated for him like the moon on a full moon night. Do you know why this verse was revealed: ‘For him is a miserable life.’ Do you know what a miserable life is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: The punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, ninety-nine dragons are set upon him. Do you know what a dragon is? Ninety-nine snakes, each snake has seven heads. They blow into his body and sting and scratch him until the Day of Resurrection.” Its chain of transmission is very strange. Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi told us: Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Hisham ibn Saad told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Ibn Hijra, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Then he will have a miserable life. He said: The miserable life about which God said that ninety-nine snakes will be set upon him, which will devour his flesh until the Hour comes. He also said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Abu al-Walid told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then he will have a miserable life. He said: The torment of the grave. A good chain of transmission. And his saying: And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. Mujahid, Abu Salih, and As-Suddi said: There is no proof for him. Ikrimah said: Everything will be blind to him except Hell. It is possible that what is meant is that he will be resurrected or gathered to Hell blind in sight and insight as well, as God Almighty said: “And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb, and deaf. Their refuge will be Hell.” This is why he says: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind while I was seeing? That is, in this world. “He will say: ‘Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot them. And thus today you will be forgotten.’” That is, when you turned away from the signs of God and treated them as one who did not remember them after they were conveyed to you, you forgot them, turned away from them, and neglected them. Thus today We will treat you as one who forgets you. So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs. For the reward is of the same kind as the action. Then Imam Ahmad narrated it from the hadith of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, on the authority of ‘Isa ibn Fa’id, on the authority of ‘Ubadah ibn as-Samit, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he mentioned something similar.
20:127: God Almighty says: And thus we reward the transgressors who deny the signs of God in this world and the Hereafter. For them is a punishment in the life of this world, and the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe, and they have no protector from God. That is why He said: And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting. That is, more painful than the punishment of this world and more lasting for them, as they will remain in it forever. That is why the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to those who cursed: The punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter.
20:128: The Almighty says: Have they not been guided to these deniers of what you have brought them, O Muhammad, how many nations of deniers of the messengers We destroyed before them, so they perished and there is no remnant, nor eye, nor trace for them, as they see that from their empty homes in which they left them, walking in them. Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding meaning sound minds and upright intellects, as the Almighty said: Have they not traveled through the land and had hearts by which to reason or ears by which to hear? Indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts. And He said in Surat Al-Sajdah: Have they not been guided how many generations We destroyed before them who walked about in their dwellings the verse, then the Almighty said: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been binding and a specified term meaning had it not been for the previous word from God, which is that He does not punish anyone except after the proof has been established against him, and the specified term that God Almighty has set for these deniers until a specific period, the punishment would have come to them. Suddenly, and for this reason he said to his Prophet, comforting him: So be patient over what they say, meaning their denial of you, and exalt the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun, meaning the dawn prayer, and before its setting, meaning the afternoon prayer, as it came in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, who said: “We were sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon, and he said: You will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in praying before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so.” Then he recited this verse. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, on the authority of Ammarah ibn Ru’aybah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No one who prays before sunrise and before sunset will enter Hell. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, and in al-Musnad and al-Sunan on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The lowest in status of the people of Paradise is he who looks at his kingdom for a distance of two thousand years, looking at its farthest point as he looks at its nearest point. The highest in status of them is he who looks at God Almighty twice a day.” And His saying: And during the hours of the night, glorify God meaning during its hours, so perform the night prayer. Some of them interpreted it as Maghrib and Isha, and at the ends of the day in contrast to the hours of the night that you may be satisfied as God the Almighty said: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied. And in the Sahih: “God the Almighty says: O people of Paradise, and they say: At Your service, our Lord, and at Your pleasure. He says: Are you satisfied? They say: Our Lord, why should we not be satisfied when You have given us what You have not given to any of Your creation? He says: I will give you better than that. They say: What is better than that? He says: I will make My pleasure descend upon you, and I will never be angry with you after that.” And in another hadith: “O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with God that He wants to fulfill for you. They say: What is it? Did He not whiten our faces, make our scales heavy, remove us from the Fire, and admit us into Paradise? He removes the veil and they look at Him, and by God, He has not given them anything better than looking at Him, which is the increase.”

20:131: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not look at the luxury that these luxurious people and their likes and counterparts enjoy, for it is only a fleeting flower and a passing blessing, so that We may test them with this, and few of My servants are grateful. Mujahid said: Wives from among them, meaning the rich, for He has given you better than what He has given them, as He said in the other verse: “And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses and the great Qur’an. Do not let your eyes yearn for [something]” (al-Baqarah 2:17). Likewise, what God Almighty has stored for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Hereafter is a great matter that cannot be limited or described, as God Almighty said: And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied. For this reason He said: And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. In the Sahih, when Umar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that room where he had isolated himself from his wives when he had sworn an oath from them, he saw him lying on a mat of sand, and there was nothing in the house except a heap of dried dates and hanging palm fronds, so Umar’s eyes began to weep, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What makes you weep, O Umar? He said: O Messenger of God, Khosrow and Caesar are in what they are in, and you are the chosen one of God’s creation? He said: Are you in doubt, O Ibn al-Khattab? Those are people. He hastened for them their good things in their worldly life.” So, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was the most ascetic of people in this world, even though he had the ability to have it. If he had it, he would spend it thus and thus on the servants of God, and he would not save anything for himself for tomorrow. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Malik informed me, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What I fear most for you is the adornment of this world that God will open for you. They said: What are the adornments of this world, O Messenger of God? He said: The blessings of the earth. Qatada and As-Suddi said: The adornment of this worldly life, meaning the adornment of this worldly life. Qatada said: To test them therein means to try them. His statement: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein means save them from the punishment of God by establishing prayer, and be constant in doing it, as God, the Most High, said: O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Salih told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Hisham ibn Sa`d told me on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of his father that Umar ibn al-Khattab and I would spend the night with him, and he would have an hour of the night in which he would pray, but he would sometimes not get up, so we would say: He does not get up at night as he used to get up. And when he woke up, he would get up, meaning his family, and he said: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it. His statement: We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you means that if you establish prayer, provision will come to you from where you do not expect, as God the Almighty said: “And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. And will provide for him from where he does not expect.” And God the Almighty said: “And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, it is God who is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy.” For this reason He said: We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. Al-Thawri said: We do not ask you for provision, meaning We do not burden you with what you ask. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, that when he entered upon the people of this world and saw a part of their worldly life, then when he returned to his family and entered the house, he would recite: “And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them - the splendor of the life of this world - that We may test them thereby. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein. We ask not of you provision; We provide for you.” Then he would say: “Prayer. Prayer, may God have mercy on you.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani told us, Sayyar told us, Jaafar told us on the authority of Thabit, who said: “Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was afflicted with poverty, he would call out to his family: ‘O my family, pray, pray.’” Thabit said: Whenever a matter befell the prophets, they would resort to prayer. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Imran bin Zaidah, from his father, from Abu Khalid al-Walibi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship, and I will fill your chest with contentment and satisfy your poverty. If you do not do so, I will fill your chest with preoccupation and will not satisfy your poverty.” Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Dahhak, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas`ud: I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever makes his worries one worry, the worry of the afterlife, God will suffice him in his worldly worries. Whoever is distracted by his worries in worldly affairs, God will not care in which valley he perishes.” It was also narrated from the hadith of Shu`bah, from `Umar bin Sulayman, from `Abd al-Rahman bin Abaan, from his father, from Zayd bin Thabit: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever’s concern is the world, God will scatter his affairs, place his poverty before his eyes, and nothing will come to him from the world except what was written for him. Whoever’s intention is the Hereafter, He will gather He has his command and made his wealth in his heart, and the world came to him reluctantly.” And his saying: And the good end is for piety means and the good end in this world and the hereafter, and it is Paradise for whoever fears God. And in the Sahih it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw last night as if we were in the house of Uqbah bin Rafi’, and we were brought dates from Ibn Tab, so I interpreted that to mean that the good end is for us in this world and elevation, and that our religion has become good.”

But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein. We ask not of you provision; We provide for you.” Then he would say: “Prayer. Prayer, may God have mercy on you.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad al-Qatwani told us, Sayyar told us, Jaafar told us on the authority of Thabit, who said: “Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was afflicted with poverty, he would call out to his family: ‘O my family, pray, pray.’” Thabit said: Whenever a matter befell the prophets, they would resort to prayer. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Imran bin Zaidah, from his father, from Abu Khalid al-Walibi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship, and I will fill your chest with contentment and satisfy your poverty. If you do not do so, I will fill your chest with preoccupation and will not satisfy your poverty.” Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Dahhak, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas`ud: I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever makes his worries one worry, the worry of the afterlife, God will suffice him in his worldly worries. Whoever is distracted by his worries in worldly affairs, God will not care in which valley he perishes.” It was also narrated from the hadith of Shu`bah, from `Umar bin Sulayman, from `Abd al-Rahman bin Abaan, from his father, from Zayd bin Thabit: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever’s concern is the world, God will scatter his affairs, place his poverty before his eyes, and nothing will come to him from the world except what was written for him. Whoever’s intention is the Hereafter, He will gather He has his command and made his wealth in his heart, and the world came to him reluctantly.” And his saying: And the good end is for piety means and the good end in this world and the hereafter, and it is Paradise for whoever fears God. And in the Sahih it is narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw last night as if we were in the house of Uqbah bin Rafi’, and we were brought dates from Ibn Tab, so I interpreted that to mean that the good end is for us in this world and elevation, and that our religion has become good.”
20:133: God Almighty says, informing us about the infidels in their saying: Why does not Muhammad bring us a sign from his Lord, that is, a sign indicating his truthfulness that he is the Messenger of God? God the Almighty said: Did there not come to them clear evidence of what was in the former scriptures? meaning the Qur’an that God revealed to him, and he was illiterate and could not write and did not study the People of the Book, and in it came the report of the ancients about what happened to them in the past, in accordance with the previous authentic books among them, for the Qur’an dominates them, confirms what is authentic and shows the error of what is false in them and against them. This verse is like the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Ankabut 29:“And they say, ‘Why were signs not sent down to him from his Lord?’ Say, ‘The signs are only with God, and I am only a clear warner.’ Was it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.” And in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “There is no prophet who was not given signs that people believed in the like of, and what I was given was only a revelation that God revealed to me, so I hope that I will have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection.” And what is mentioned here is the greatest signs that were given to him, peace be upon him, which is the Qur’an, otherwise he has miracles that are limitless and innumerable, as is deposited in his books and established in Its locations. Then the Almighty said: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, ‘Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger?’ That is, if We had destroyed these deniers before We sent to them this noble Messenger and revealed to them this great Book, they would have said, Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger? before You destroyed us so that we would believe in him and follow him, as He said: So that we would follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced. The Almighty clarifies that these deniers are stubborn and obstinate and do not believe, even if every sign came to them until they saw the painful punishment, as the Almighty said: And this is a blessed Book We have revealed, so follow it and fear God that you may receive mercy. to His saying, because of what they used to turn away. And He said: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the nations. The verse, and He said: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. The two verses, then the Almighty said: Say, that is, O Muhammad, to those who denied you and opposed you and persisted in their disbelief and obstinacy, Every “Waiting means from us and from you. Wait means wait. Then you will know who are the people of the straight path meaning the straight road and who is guided to the truth and the path of righteousness. This is like the Almighty’s saying: And they will know when they see the punishment who is most astray in way and He said: They will know tomorrow who is the most evil liar. The last interpretation of Surat Taha, praise and thanks be to God, and it will be followed, God willing, by the interpretation of Surat Al-Anbiya, praise be to God.
